definition_zh: 流行音乐；砰的一声；爆开；突然冒出；匆匆去一趟
definition_en: popular music as a genre; a short sharp bursting sound; to burst or open with such a sound; and to appear or go somewhere suddenly
core_image: 手臂边一只气球突然炸开，碎片飞出去，屋里的人全都抬头
scene: 街角的小店门口挂着旧音箱，午后的阳光斜进来，一群学生跟着旋律点头。The radio kept playing one pop song after another while the students waited for the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 pop 指「流行音乐」（第 1 个义项：旋律好记、面向大众的音乐）；句意为学生们等公交时，收音机一首接一首地放着流行歌。图中可辨识物件：旧音箱、斜照进来的阳光、等车的学生。

pos.zh: 流行音乐；砰的一声
爆开；突然冒出；匆匆去一趟
流行音乐的；通俗的

derivatives.zh: 由 pop 与 corn 复合而成，取「受热爆开」的旧义，义为「爆米花」
由 pop 加表示工具或人的 -er 构成，义为「爆米花锅；按扣」
由 pop 加 -ing 构成，义为「连续的爆响；机械舞」

senses.title: Popular music as a genre
senses.definition: a style of music with a strong beat and easily remembered tunes, made for a wide audience rather than for specialists
senses.definitionCN: 节奏鲜明、旋律好记，面向广大听众而非专业圈子的音乐类型
senses.example: She sang along to every pop song on the radio.
senses.exampleCN: 收音机里每一首流行歌她都跟着唱。
senses.why: This sense is a mid-twentieth-century clipping of popular, taken from phrases such as popular music, so the name says who the music is made for rather than how it is composed.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是二十世纪中叶从 popular 截短来的，取的是 popular music 一类说法，所以名字说的是音乐做给谁听，而不是它怎么写。

senses.title: A short sharp bursting sound
senses.definition: a small explosive noise made when something bursts, snaps or is struck
senses.definitionCN: 东西爆开、绷断或被击中时发出的短促爆响
senses.example: The paper bag gave a loud pop when she hit it.
senses.exampleCN: 她一巴掌拍下去，纸袋砰地响了一声。
senses.why: This sense is generally taken to be imitative: the word copies the noise of a small burst, which is why one form can name both the sound and the event behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项一般认为来自拟声：词本身在模仿小东西爆开的声响，所以同一种形式既能指声音，也能指发出声音的那件事。

senses.title: To burst or open with a sharp sound
senses.definition: to burst, open or come out suddenly with a small sharp noise
senses.definitionCN: 伴随着短促响声突然爆开、弹开或冒出来
senses.example: The cork popped out of the bottle and hit the ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶塞砰地从瓶口弹出来，撞到了天花板上。
senses.why: Once the sound-word had named the noise of bursting, English could turn it into a verb for whatever produced that noise, and a cork leaving a bottle is the clearest case.
senses.whyCN: 拟声词一旦指认了爆裂的响声，英语就能把它变成动词，指发出这声响的东西；瓶塞飞出瓶口就是最清楚的例子。

senses.title: To appear or go somewhere suddenly
senses.definition: to come into view suddenly and briefly, or to go somewhere quickly for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 突然而短暂地出现在眼前，或很快地去某处一趟
senses.example: A rabbit popped out of the hole and froze.
senses.exampleCN: 一只兔子突然从洞里冒出来，随即定住不动。
senses.why: A burst is sudden and over in a moment; English carries that suddenness over to anything that appears or leaves in a flash, which is how the verb reaches rabbits and short errands.
senses.whyCN: 爆开是一下子发生、一下就结束的；英语把这种突然挪到任何一闪而现或一闪而去的事情上，动词于是能用来说兔子，也能说匆匆跑一趟。

intro.en: English has two words written pop: an imitative syllable for a bang, and a twentieth-century clipping of popular. The spellings merged, the histories did not.
intro.cn: 英语里有两个拼作 pop 的词：一个模仿爆响，一个是二十世纪对 popular 的截短。拼写合流了，来历并没有合流。

items.en: Populus named the people as a body, the crowd whose taste decides what becomes common.
items.cn: populus 指作为整体的民众，也就是他们的喜好决定了什么东西会变得普遍。

items.en: Popularis meant belonging to or pleasing the people, and it is the adjective that pop would later shorten.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的、讨民众喜欢的，正是后来被 pop 截短的那个形容词。

items.en: Generally regarded as imitative, the short word for a small explosion copies the sound itself and has no connection with Latin.
items.cn: 一般认为表示小爆炸的 pop 是拟声词，直接模仿声音，与拉丁语没有关系。

items.en: In the mid-twentieth century popular music was clipped to pop, used first as a modifier and soon as a noun in its own right.
items.cn: 二十世纪中叶，popular music 被截短成 pop，先作修饰语，很快又独立作名词。

items.en: Modern English keeps both strands: a bang, a quick errand and a whole shelf of music, all spelled the same way.
items.cn: 现代英语两条线都留着：一声爆响、一趟快去快回、一整排音乐，拼写完全一样。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the populus family behind the music sense; the near-meaning group collects other words for popular music and for sudden movement.
note.cn: 形近组顺着音乐义背后的 populus 词族展开；近义组收表示流行音乐与突然动作的其他词。

entries.definition: Liked by many people; the adjective that pop shortens.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱的；pop 正是它的截短形式。

entries.definition: The state of being liked or accepted by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱或接受的状况。

entries.definition: To make something widely known or liked.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物广为人知或广受欢迎。

entries.definition: Corn that bursts open when it is heated.
entries.definitionCN: 受热后爆开的玉米；爆米花。

entries.definition: A loud form of popular music built on guitars and drums.
entries.definitionCN: 以吉他和鼓为主的吵闹流行音乐；摇滚。

entries.definition: A song or record that becomes very successful.
entries.definitionCN: 非常成功的歌曲或唱片；热门歌曲。

entries.definition: The music, taste or opinion accepted by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 被大多数人接受的音乐、品味或观点；主流。

normalIntro.en: The word carries two histories at once: a copied sound and a shortened adjective, and most of its uses can be traced to one or the other.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时背着两段来历：一个模仿来的声音，一个被截短的形容词；它的用法大多能归到其中一条。

normal.en: Popular music was shortened to pop, so a pop song is simply a song meant for everybody.
normal.cn: popular music 被缩成 pop，所以 pop song 就是给所有人听的歌。

normal.en: The bang is imitative: say the word sharply and you have already made the sound.
normal.cn: 爆响那个义项是拟声的：把这个词短促地念出来，声音就已经发出来了。

normal.en: Pop up keeps the idea of a burst: something appears as if it had just exploded into view.
normal.cn: pop up 保留了「突然爆开」的意思：某物像是刚炸出来一样出现在眼前。

normal.en: Pop into a shop applies the same suddenness to a short errand, in and out in a moment.
normal.cn: pop into a shop 把同一种突然用在短程跑腿上，进去又出来，只用一会儿。

normal.en: Popcorn is named for the moment the kernel bursts, so the compound preserves the oldest sense.
normal.cn: popcorn 得名于玉米粒爆开的那一刻，这个复合词保存了最古老的义项。

abstract.en: One syllable carries both a drum hit and a hit song: noise and culture share a spelling.
abstract.cn: 一个音节既装着鼓点的一击，也装着一首热门歌：声音和文化共用一种拼写。

abstract.en: A balloon, a cork, a rabbit: the same snap marks every sudden appearance.
abstract.cn: 气球、瓶塞、兔子：同一声脆响标记着每一次突然出现。

abstract.en: Pop is what a crowd makes common, so the word for the people sits silently inside it.
abstract.cn: pop 指人群使之变得普遍的东西，所以表示民众的那个词静静藏在它里面。

examples.en: The children danced to a pop song in the kitchen.
examples.cn: 孩子们在厨房里跟着一首流行歌跳舞。

examples.en: The balloon popped and the dog ran off.
examples.cn: 气球砰地爆了，狗跑开了。

examples.en: A message popped up on the screen.
examples.cn: 屏幕上突然弹出一条消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡泡」——泡泡一破就是砰的一声；pop 又是人人会哼的流行歌。

root: 一般认为有两个来源：表示爆响的 pop 是拟声词；表示流行音乐的 pop 是 popular 的截短形式，而 popular 出自拉丁语 populus（民众）。

sensesIntro.en: Two origins feed one spelling: the sharp sound and its suddenness on one side, mass-market music on the other.
sensesIntro.cn: 两种来历汇成一个拼写：一边是爆响与随之而来的突然，另一边是面向大众的音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon bursting at arm's length, its skin flying off while everyone looks up.
core.cn: 核心意象：手臂边上一只气球突然炸开，碎片飞出去，所有人都抬头看。

branches.en: a phone playing a three-minute song at full volume
branches.cn: 手机以最大音量放一首三分钟的歌

branches.en: a paper bag bursting under a slap
branches.cn: 一巴掌拍破的纸袋

branches.en: a cork flying across the kitchen
branches.cn: 瓶塞飞过厨房

branches.en: someone dashing into a shop for milk
branches.cn: 有人冲进小店买牛奶

branches.en: one short word for a bang and for a hit tune
branches.cn: 一个短词同时指爆响和热门曲子

intro.en: The word rests on two layers: an imitative English syllable, and the Latin family of populus. In that family -ar builds the adjective popular, -ity builds the noun of state, and -ize builds the verb of making; pop itself is only a clipping of the -ar form.
intro.cn: 这个词压着两层东西：一个拟声的英语音节，以及拉丁语 populus 词族。在这个词族里，-ar 造形容词 popular，-ity 造表状态的名词，-ize 造表「使……」的动词；pop 本身只是那个 -ar 形容词的截短。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

burst with a short sharp sound

definition_zh: 受欢迎的；大众的；通俗的；民众的；普遍的
definition_en: liked or approved by many people; made for ordinary people rather than specialists; of the people as a political source; and held by most people
core_image: 小店门口排起长队，路过的人不知道卖什么，也先跟着排上
scene: 放学后的面馆门口总有人排队，队伍拐过墙角，连附近上班的人也来凑热闹。That noodle shop is popular with students because it is cheap and fast.
sceneCN: 这里 popular 指「受欢迎的」（第 1 个义项：被很多人喜欢）；句意为这家面馆便宜又上得快，很受学生欢迎。图中可辨识场景：排到墙角的长队、放学的学生、探头张望的路人。

pos.zh: 受欢迎的；大众的；通俗的；民众的；普遍的

derivatives.zh: 由 popular 加 -ity 构成，义为「受欢迎；人气」
由 popular 加 -ize 构成，义为「使普及；使通俗化」
由 popular 加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地；由民众」
由 popular 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不受欢迎的」

senses.title: Liked by many people
senses.definition: liked, approved of or supported by a large number of people
senses.definitionCN: 被很多人喜欢、认可或支持的
senses.example: The new teacher quickly became popular with her class.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的老师很快就受到班上学生的欢迎。
senses.why: Latin popularis meant belonging to the people; a thing that belongs to everybody is one everybody is ready to accept, so approval grows out of that shared ownership.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 popularis 意为属于民众的；一样东西既然属于所有人，大家就都愿意接受它，「受欢迎」正是从这种共有关系里长出来的。

senses.title: Made for ordinary people
senses.definition: designed for ordinary people rather than for experts, and therefore easy to follow
senses.definitionCN: 面向普通人而非专家，因而容易听懂的
senses.example: He writes popular books about astronomy for readers with no training.
senses.exampleCN: 他写的天文读物面向没有受过专业训练的读者。
senses.why: If something is of the people, it is also for the people, so the word came to mark work that avoids the language of specialists.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西属于民众，自然也是做给民众的，于是这个词用来标记那些避开专家术语的作品。

senses.title: Of the people as a political source
senses.definition: relating to ordinary citizens, especially as the source of political authority
senses.definitionCN: 与普通公民有关的，尤指权力来自他们的
senses.example: The constitution was approved by a popular vote.
senses.exampleCN: 这部宪法经民众投票获得通过。
senses.why: The oldest political sense keeps the Latin meaning almost untouched: authority rests with populus, the people, not with a ruler above them.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的政治义几乎原封不动保留了拉丁含义：权力属于 populus（民众），而不是属于高居于他们之上的统治者。

senses.title: Held by most people
senses.definition: believed or repeated by a large part of the public, whether or not it is true
senses.definitionCN: 被大部分公众相信或传说的，不论真假
senses.example: It is a popular belief that we only use ten percent of our brains.
senses.exampleCN: 人们普遍相信我们只用了大脑的百分之十。
senses.why: Once an idea belongs to the many, it counts as popular even when it is wrong, which is why the word can sit directly beside belief and misconception.
senses.whyCN: 一个说法一旦属于很多人，即使它是错的也被称作 popular，所以这个词能直接修饰「看法」和「误解」。

intro.en: Popular came from Latin through French with the plain sense of belonging to the people; only later did English add the warmer sense of being liked.
intro.cn: popular 经法语来自拉丁语，本义只是「属于民众的」；「受喜爱」这层更暖的意思是很晚才由英语添上的。

items.en: Populus was the body of citizens, the people seen as a single crowd.
items.cn: populus 指公民的整体，是把人们看作一群人。

items.en: Popularis meant belonging to, pleasing or favouring the people, and it could describe a politician who courted them.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的、讨民众喜欢的、站在民众一边的，也能形容讨好民众的政治人物。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as populaire, keeping both the neutral and the approving tones.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 populaire，中性义与赞许义都保留着。

items.en: Middle English populere meant common, of the common people, and could still carry a hint of vulgar.
items.cn: 中古英语的 populere 意为普通的、平民的，仍可能带一点「粗俗」的意味。

items.en: Modern English pushed the word towards approval and, in politics, towards the people as the source of authority.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义推向「受认可」，在政治语境里则推向「权力来自民众」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the populus family and its negated form; the near-meaning group gathers words for being widely known or widely held.
note.cn: 形近组收 populus 词族及其否定形式；近义组收表示广为人知、广为接受的词。

entries.definition: The state or degree of being liked by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱的状态或程度。

entries.definition: To make something widely known, used or liked.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物广为人知、广为使用或广受欢迎。

entries.definition: Full of people; having a large population.
entries.definitionCN: 人口众多的；人烟稠密的。

entries.definition: Not liked or approved of by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 不被大多数人喜欢的；不受欢迎的。

entries.definition: Known by a great many people.
entries.definitionCN: 被很多人知道的；著名的。

entries.definition: Found, done or believed by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 大多数人都有的、做的或相信的；常见的。

entries.definition: Existing or happening over a large area or among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大范围或许多人中存在的；普遍的。

normalIntro.en: The word begins with a Latin noun for the people, and each modern sense measures some way in which a thing belongs to them.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起于拉丁语里表示民众的名词，每个现代义项都在衡量某样东西以何种方式属于他们。

normal.en: Latin popularis meant of the people, and being liked is simply being accepted by the people who own it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 popularis 意为属于民众的，而「被喜欢」不过是被拥有它的那群人接受。

normal.en: Popular and population share populus: one counts approval, the other counts heads.
normal.cn: popular 与 population 共用 populus：一个数的是认可，一个数的是人头。

normal.en: Popularity is popular plus -ity, the state of being liked seen as a quantity.
normal.cn: popularity 是 popular 加 -ity，把「被喜欢」看成一种可计量的状态。

normal.en: Popularize is popular plus -ize, to make something common among people.
normal.cn: popularize 是 popular 加 -ize，让某样东西在人们中间变得普遍。

normal.en: Popular with names the crowd that likes it; popular for names the reason.
normal.cn: popular with 后面接喜欢它的人群；popular for 后面接喜欢它的原因。

abstract.en: A queue outside a small shop is popularity made visible.
abstract.cn: 小店门口的一条长队，就是看得见的人气。

abstract.en: What belongs to everyone ends up pleasing everyone, so ownership turns into affection.
abstract.cn: 属于所有人的东西，最后会让所有人喜欢，所有权就这样变成了好感。

abstract.en: A word can be popular and still be wrong, which is why belief takes the same adjective as music.
abstract.cn: 一个说法可以很流行又完全是错的，所以「看法」和音乐共用同一个形容词。

examples.en: This song is popular with children.
examples.cn: 这首歌很受孩子们欢迎。

examples.en: Popular science books explain hard ideas in plain words.
examples.cn: 科普读物用平实的语言解释难懂的概念。

examples.en: The mayor was elected by popular vote.
examples.cn: 市长是通过民众投票选出的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡普乐」——把知识泡进普通人的快乐里，大家就都喜欢；popular 就是受欢迎的、大众的。

root: 拉丁语 populus（民众）→ popularis（属于民众的）→ 古法语 populaire → 英语 popular；同族还有 population、populace。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is belonging to the people; it then splits into being liked, being made for them, coming from them politically, and being believed by them.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「属于民众」；由此分出被他们喜欢、为他们而做、政治上来自他们，以及被他们相信。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue curling round the corner of a small shop, strangers joining it without asking why.
core.cn: 核心意象：小店门口的长队拐过墙角，陌生人没问缘由也排了进去。

branches.en: a queue curling round the corner of a noodle shop
branches.cn: 绕着面馆墙角的长队

branches.en: a plain-language guide to the stars on a bestseller table
branches.cn: 畅销书台上那本讲星星的通俗读物

branches.en: a ballot box where each citizen counts once
branches.cn: 每位公民都只算一票的投票箱

branches.en: a saying repeated in every kitchen and every office
branches.cn: 每个厨房和办公室都在重复的一句老话

branches.en: a leader who is both liked and chosen
branches.cn: 既被喜欢又被选出来的领导人

intro.en: A Latin noun for the people and its adjective carry the word, and the English suffixes divide the labour: -ar makes the adjective, -ity the noun of state, -ize the verb of making.
intro.cn: 一个表示民众的拉丁名词及其形容词撑起这个词，英语后缀则各管一段：-ar 造形容词，-ity 造表状态的名词，-ize 造表「使……」的动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 受欢迎；人气；普及程度；声望
definition_en: the state of being liked or supported by many people, and the degree to which something is widely accepted
core_image: 一块电子屏上的数字不断往上跳，屏幕前的店主抬头看了三次
scene: 新开的面包店在社交平台上被反复转发，门口的队伍从早到晚没有断过。The popularity of the little bakery surprised even its owner.
sceneCN: 这里 popularity 指「受欢迎的程度」（第 1 个义项：被很多人喜欢的状况）；句意为这家小面包店的火爆连店主自己都感到意外。图中可辨识场景：不断上涨的数字、从早排到晚的队伍、反复转发的手机屏幕。

pos.zh: 受欢迎；人气；普及程度；声望

derivatives.zh: 由 popularity 去掉名词后缀 -ity 得到，义为「受欢迎的；大众的」
由 popular 加 -ize 构成，义为「使普及；使通俗化」
由 popularity 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不受欢迎」
由 popular 加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地；由民众」

senses.title: The state of being liked
senses.definition: the fact or condition of being liked, approved of or supported by many people
senses.definitionCN: 被很多人喜欢、认可或支持的状态
senses.example: Her popularity among younger readers grew with each new book.
senses.exampleCN: 随着每本新书出版，她在年轻读者中越来越受欢迎。
senses.why: The Latin noun popularitas first named the condition of being one of the people; being counted among them later turned into being favoured by them, and -ity fixed that favour as a state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 popularitas 最初指「身为民众一员」的状态；后来「被算作他们中间的人」变成「被他们偏爱」，后缀 -ity 又把这份偏爱固定成一种状态。

senses.title: The degree to which something is widespread
senses.definition: how widely a product, idea or activity is used or accepted by the public
senses.definitionCN: 某产品、观念或活动被公众使用、接受得有多广
senses.example: The popularity of online courses has changed how adults study.
senses.exampleCN: 网络课程的普及改变了成年人学习的方式。
senses.why: If belonging to the people can be shared by a habit as well as by a person, then the word can measure how far that habit has spread among them.
senses.whyCN: 既然「属于民众」既可以是人，也可以是一种习惯，这个词就能用来衡量这种习惯在他们中间扩散了多远。

senses.title: Public standing, often competed for
senses.definition: the position a person or group holds in public favour, especially when it is won, lost or competed for
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体在公众好感中所处的位置，尤指需要争取、会失去、会被比较的
senses.example: The two singers fought for popularity on the weekly chart.
senses.exampleCN: 两位歌手在每周榜单上争夺人气。
senses.why: Once liking can be counted it can be compared, and what can be compared can be contested, so the word shifts from a feeling to a ranking that people chase.
senses.whyCN: 喜欢一旦可以计数就能比较，能比较就能争夺，于是这个词从一种感受变成人人追逐的排名。

intro.en: Popularity is a Latin noun of shared citizenship that English turned into a measure of public favour.
intro.cn: popularity 本是拉丁语中表示「同属民众」的名词，英语把它变成了衡量公众好感的尺子。

items.en: Populus was the body of citizens, the crowd whose approval gave a word its weight.
items.cn: populus 指公民整体，是他们的认可给了某个说法分量。

items.en: Popularis meant of the people, and in Roman politics it described the side that courted them.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的，在罗马政治里指讨好民众的那一派。

items.en: Popularitas named the state of being one of the people, and by extension the favour that came with standing among them.
items.cn: popularitas 指身为民众一员的状态，进而指站在他们中间所获得的拥护。

items.en: French popularité carried the noun towards public favour, and English borrowed it in that warmer sense.
items.cn: 法语 popularité 把这个名词推向「公众好感」，英语借入时接受的就是这层更暖的意思。

items.en: Modern English made it countable and comparable, adding phrases such as popularity contest and ratings of popularity.
items.cn: 现代英语让它可数、可比较，于是有了 popularity contest 和各类人气排行。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the populus family and the noun built on it; the near-meaning group gathers words for public standing and renown.
note.cn: 形近组收 populus 词族及由它构成的名词；近义组收表示公众地位与名声的词。

entries.definition: Liked or accepted by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜欢或接受的。

entries.definition: To make something widely known or liked.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物广为人知或广受欢迎。

entries.definition: The act of making an idea or subject widely known.
entries.definitionCN: 使观念或学科广为人知的行为；普及。

entries.definition: A politician who claims to speak for ordinary people.
entries.definitionCN: 自称代表普通民众的政治人物；民粹主义者。

entries.definition: The state of being known by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 被许多人知道的状态；名声。

entries.definition: The opinion people generally have of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 人们普遍对某人或某物的看法；名声。

entries.definition: A person's rank or status in the eyes of others.
entries.definitionCN: 在他人眼中的地位或等级。

normalIntro.en: This word is the Latin noun of belonging-to-the-people, later narrowed into the amount of favour a person or thing enjoys.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语里「同属民众」的名词，后来收窄为某人或某物享有的好感有多少。

normal.en: Popularitas in Latin named the condition of being one of the people, not being liked; the modern sense is a later narrowing.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 popularitas 指身为民众一员的状态，而不是被喜欢；现代义是后来收窄的结果。

normal.en: Popularity is popular plus -ity, so the word names a state and never a person.
normal.cn: popularity 是 popular 加 -ity，所以它指一种状态，从不指人。

normal.en: You gain, lose or measure popularity because it is treated as a quantity.
normal.cn: 你会获得、失去或衡量 popularity，因为它被当成一个量。

normal.en: Popularity contest is a twentieth-century phrase from school and media life, where liking turns into a score.
normal.cn: popularity contest 是二十世纪从校园与媒体生活里来的说法，喜欢在那里变成了分数。

normal.en: Unpopularity adds un- to the same noun and keeps the same countable feel.
normal.cn: unpopularity 在同一名词前加 un-，仍然保留那种可计量的感觉。

abstract.en: A number climbing on a screen is a feeling that has been turned into a score.
abstract.cn: 屏幕上不断攀升的数字，是一种被换算成分数的感受。

abstract.en: To belong to a crowd and to be loved by it are two steps of the same walk.
abstract.cn: 属于一群人，与被这群人喜爱，是同一段路的两个台阶。

abstract.en: Popularity measures how far a thing has travelled, not how good it is.
abstract.cn: popularity 衡量的是某样东西走了多远，而不是它有多好。

examples.en: The band's popularity has grown since the tour.
examples.cn: 巡演之后，这支乐队的人气上升了。

examples.en: Critics questioned the popularity of the new format.
examples.cn: 评论者质疑这种新形式的流行程度。

examples.en: He won popularity by listening more than speaking.
examples.cn: 他靠多听少说赢得了人心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡普乐了题」——一道题在普通人里传开，人人都聊，就是 popularity：人气、普及。

root: 拉丁语 popularitas（公民身份、公众好感）← popularis（属于民众的）← populus（民众）；后缀 -ity 表示状态。

sensesIntro.en: From shared citizenship the noun narrows to being liked, then widens to how far something has spread, and finally to the standing people compete for.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从「同属民众」收窄到「被喜欢」，再扩展到「扩散得多远」，最后落到人们争抢的地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number on a screen climbing while the shopkeeper looks up at it again and again.
core.cn: 核心意象：屏幕上的数字不断往上跳，店主一次又一次抬头看它。

branches.en: a reader queueing for a signed copy
branches.cn: 排队等签售的读者

branches.en: a course catalogue that keeps growing
branches.cn: 不断加长的课程目录

branches.en: two names trading places on a weekly chart
branches.cn: 每周榜单上互换位置的两个名字

branches.en: a singer whose likeability becomes a ranking
branches.cn: 歌手的讨喜程度变成一项排名

branches.en: a format that spreads and is then ranked
branches.cn: 一种形式先传开，随后被排名

intro.en: A Latin noun of citizenship, its adjective and its suffix supply the stem. Here -ar belongs to the adjective, -ity builds this noun of state, and -ize would build the verb of making.
intro.cn: 一个表示公民身份的拉丁名词、它的形容词与后缀提供词干。这里 -ar 属于形容词，-ity 造出这个表状态的名词，-ize 则用来造表「使……」的动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the state of not being liked

definition_zh: 使普及；使流行；使通俗易懂；推广
definition_en: to make something widely known, used or liked, especially by presenting it in a form ordinary people can understand
core_image: 一位老师把厚书上的公式拆成几张手绘图，贴在菜市场门口的黑板上
scene: 社区活动室里，退休工程师把复杂的电路画成几笔简图，围坐的老人边听边点头。His talks helped popularize basic electronics among people who had never opened a machine.
sceneCN: 这里 popularize 指「使通俗易懂并广为流传」（第 2 个义项：把专门内容讲到普通人也能懂）；句意为他的讲座让从没拆过机器的人也能听懂基础电子知识。图中可辨识场景：活动室里的简图、围坐的老人、点头的动作。

pos.zh: 使普及；使流行；使通俗易懂；推广

derivatives.zh: 由 popularize 加 -ation 构成，义为「普及；通俗化」
由 popularize 加 -er 构成，义为「普及者；推广者」
由 popularize 去掉动词后缀 -ize 得到，义为「大众的；受欢迎的」
由 popular 加 -ity 构成，义为「受欢迎；人气」

senses.title: To make something widely known and used
senses.definition: to cause an idea, product or practice to become known and used by a large number of ordinary people
senses.definitionCN: 使观念、产品或做法被大量普通人知道并使用
senses.example: Cheap printing helped popularize the novel in the nineteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价印刷在十九世纪推动了小说的普及。
senses.why: Popularize is popular plus -ize, a suffix meaning to make something have a quality; to popularize is therefore to make a thing belong to the people.
senses.whyCN: popularize 是 popular 加 -ize，这个后缀表示使某物具有某种性质；所以「使普及」就是让某样东西归到民众手里。

senses.title: To present specialist material in plain terms
senses.definition: to explain a technical or academic subject in language that non-specialists can follow
senses.definitionCN: 用非专业者也能跟上的语言解释技术或学术内容
senses.example: The series popularized astronomy without watering down the science.
senses.exampleCN: 这套节目普及了天文知识，却没有把科学内容兑水。
senses.why: If a subject is to belong to everybody, its language has to leave the laboratory, so the verb also names the work of turning jargon into plain speech.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问要属于所有人，它的语言就得走出实验室，于是这个动词也用来指把术语翻成大白话的那份工作。

senses.title: To promote something to the public
senses.definition: to market or promote a product, place or idea so that ordinary people accept it
senses.definitionCN: 为产品、地点或观念做营销宣传，使普通人接受
senses.example: The campaign popularized a drink that few people had heard of.
senses.exampleCN: 这场推广让一种很少有人听过的饮料流行起来。
senses.why: Once the verb means making a thing common, businesses borrow it for the deliberate work of pushing a product into ordinary hands.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个动词指让东西变普遍，商家就借它来指有意识地把产品推到大众人手里的工作。

intro.en: Popularize was not inherited from Latin: English built it from the adjective popular and the suffix -ize, and Latin has no verb popularizare.
intro.cn: popularize 不是从拉丁语继承来的：英语用形容词 popular 加后缀 -ize 造出它，拉丁语里并没有 popularizare 这个动词。

items.en: Populus, the people as a body, is the root behind the whole family.
items.cn: populus 指作为整体的民众，是整族词背后的根。

items.en: Popularis, of the people, supplied the stem that English later took as popular.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的，提供词干，英语后来把它取作 popular。

items.en: English borrowed popular through French and used it for what is common, public or widely liked.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入 popular，用它指公共的、大众的或广受喜爱的。

items.en: The verb ending -izein, taken into Latin as -izare and into English as -ize, means to make, do or act in a certain way.
items.cn: 动词词尾 -izein 经拉丁语 -izare 进入英语作 -ize，意为使成为、做、按某种方式行事。

items.en: English joined the two around the early nineteenth century, when cheap print and public lectures were carrying science to ordinary readers.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪初前后把两者拼在一起，那正是廉价印刷与公开讲座把科学带给普通读者的年代。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same word family, all resting on populus; the near-meaning group holds other verbs for spreading and simplifying.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个词族，都依托 populus；近义组收表示传播与简化的其他动词。

entries.definition: Liked by many people; of the people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱的；大众的。

entries.definition: The state of being liked by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱的状态。

entries.definition: The act or result of making something widely known.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物广为人知的行为或结果；普及。

entries.definition: A person who makes a subject or product widely known.
entries.definitionCN: 把学科或产品带给大众的人。

entries.definition: To cause something to reach more people or places.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物传到更多人或地方。

entries.definition: To help something grow, sell or become accepted.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助某物增长、销售或被接受；推广。

entries.definition: To make something easier to understand or do.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物更容易理解或做到。

normalIntro.en: The word is an English construction on a Latin stem, and its senses follow one line: bring something down to the level of the people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是英语在拉丁词干上造出来的，几个义项沿着一条线走：把东西带到普通人够得着的高度。

normal.en: Popularize is popular plus -ize; the suffix says make, so the verb says make it belong to the people.
normal.cn: popularize 是 popular 加 -ize；后缀表示「使」，动词的意思就是让它归到民众手里。

normal.en: There was no Latin verb popularizare; the word was built inside English from an adjective and a suffix.
normal.cn: 拉丁语里没有 popularizare 这个动词；这个词是英语用形容词加后缀造的。

normal.en: Science, theories and products are its usual objects, because all three need translating for a crowd.
normal.cn: 科学、理论和产品是它常见的对象，因为这三样都需要为大众翻译一遍。

normal.en: Popularization is the noun, popularizer the person who does it.
normal.cn: popularization 是名词，popularizer 是做这件事的人。

normal.en: The word follows the -ize pattern of modernize and globalize: make something spread.
normal.cn: 这个词沿用 modernize 与 globalize 的 -ize 模式：使某样东西扩散。

abstract.en: To popularize is to carry something heavy down the stairs to where people are standing.
abstract.cn: 普及就是把某样沉重的东西搬下楼梯，搬到人们站着的地方。

abstract.en: A diagram that replaces a page of equations has done the work the word names.
abstract.cn: 一张图替掉一页公式，就已经完成了这个词所指的那件事。

abstract.en: Making a thing common and making it liked are the same motion seen from two ends.
abstract.cn: 让东西变普遍，与让东西被喜欢，是同一个动作的两端。

examples.en: Television did more than any book to popularize the sport.
examples.cn: 电视对这项运动普及的推动超过了任何一本书。

examples.en: She popularized the method by teaching it in short videos.
examples.cn: 她用短视频讲这个方法，使它流行起来。

examples.en: The museum works to popularize local history among children.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆致力于在孩子们中间普及本地历史。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡普乐来兹」——把东西泡进普通人的快乐里，让它变得人人都会，就是 popularize：推广普及。

root: popular（大众的，源自拉丁语 populus 民众）+ 后缀 -ize（使……化）；拉丁语并无 popularizare 这一动词，popularize 是英语后造的词。

sensesIntro.en: One motion runs through the senses: take something out of the hands of specialists and put it into the hands of ordinary people.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项贯穿着同一个动作：把东西从专家手里拿出来，放到普通人手里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a teacher turning a page of formulas into a few hand-drawn arrows, pinned up where everyone walks past.
core.cn: 核心意象：老师把一页公式画成几个手绘箭头，贴在人人经过的地方。

branches.en: a cheap edition that puts a novel in every pocket
branches.cn: 让小说进到每个人口袋的廉价版本

branches.en: a diagram that turns a formula into three arrows
branches.cn: 把公式变成三个箭头的示意图

branches.en: a poster that makes a new drink look familiar
branches.cn: 让新饮料看着眼熟的海报

branches.en: a lecture that is both simple and passed on
branches.cn: 既讲得简单又被口口相传的讲座

branches.en: a plain explanation that ends up as an advertisement
branches.cn: 一段通俗讲解最终变成广告

intro.en: A Latin stem for the people meets an English suffix of making. The family divides cleanly: -ar makes the adjective, -ity the noun of state, -ize this verb of making, and -ation or -er the act and the person.
intro.cn: 表示民众的拉丁词干遇上表示「使」的英语后缀。整族词分工清楚：-ar 造形容词，-ity 造表状态的名词，-ize 造这个表「使……」的动词，-ation 与 -er 再分别指行为和做这件事的人。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

a person who makes something common

definition_zh: 人口；全体居民；种群；（统计）总体
definition_en: the people living in a place, or any group of individuals counted together, including a breeding group of animals or a complete set of data
core_image: 一张城市鸟瞰图，屋顶密密麻麻，每个小点代表一个人，远处还有一片标着虫鸟的林子
scene: 这座小城的人口在二十年间翻了一倍，供水却始终没跟上。The city's population doubled in twenty years, and the water supply never caught up.
sceneCN: 这里 population 是「人口、居民总数」（第 1 个义项：某地居民的整体数量）；句意：这座城市的人口在二十年间翻了一番，供水却始终没跟上。图中可辨识物件：密集屋顶、代表居民的小点、远处的林地与鸟群；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 人口；全体居民；种群；总体

有人居住的

senses.title: People counted together
senses.definition: the total number of people who live in a particular area, town or country
senses.definitionCN: 居住在某一地区、城镇或国家的总人数
senses.example: The population of the region passed five million last year.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的人口去年突破五百万。
senses.why: populus in Latin meant 'the people'. The suffix -ation turns the body of people into a countable quantity, so the word names people as a number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 populus 意为“人民”。后缀 -ation 把一群人变成可计数的量，因此这个词把“人”命名为一个数字。

senses.title: The people themselves
senses.titleCN: 全体居民：住在那里的人
senses.definition: all the inhabitants of a place, thought of as a social body rather than as a statistic
senses.definitionCN: 某地的全部居民，被视为一个社会群体而非一个统计数字
senses.example: The new bus route mainly serves the rural population.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新公交线路主要服务农村居民。
senses.why: English often uses population for the living community, not merely its size. The same word shifts from number to people by context alone.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用 population 指活生生的社区，而不只是它的规模。同一个词凭语境从“数字”滑向“人群”。

senses.title: A named subgroup
senses.titleCN: 特定人群：某类人构成的那一群
senses.definition: a particular group within a larger community, such as students, patients or workers
senses.definitionCN: 较大社区中的某一特定群体，如学生、病人或劳动者
senses.example: The clinic serves a mainly elderly population.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所主要服务老年人群。
senses.why: Any bounded group can be called a population because the word only requires a set of individuals and a shared boundary.
senses.whyCN: 任何有边界的群体都可称作 population，因为这个词只要求“一群个体”加“一条共同边界”。

senses.title: Biology: one breeding group
senses.definition: in biology, a group of organisms of the same species living in one area and able to interbreed
senses.definitionCN: 生物学上指同一物种、生活在同一区域且能相互交配繁殖的一群生物
senses.example: The island population of finches has been isolated for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的雀鸟种群已隔离了几个世纪。
senses.why: Biologists borrowed the demographic word and replaced 'citizens' with 'individuals of one species'. The boundary, not the species, defines the group.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借用了人口学的词，把“公民”换成“同一物种的个体”。界定群体的是边界，而不是物种。

senses.title: Statistics: the whole set
senses.titleCN: 统计学：总体（与样本相对）
senses.definition: in statistics, the complete set of items from which a sample is drawn
senses.definitionCN: 统计学上指被抽样的完整集合，与“样本”相对
senses.example: The sample was chosen randomly from a population of ten thousand firms.
senses.exampleCN: 样本是从一万家企业的总体中随机抽出的。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the demographic sense of 'everyone', then applies it to any complete set: once you can count a group, the group is a population.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留“全部人”的人口学含义，再套到任何完整集合上：只要能计数一群，这群就是总体。

senses.title: Animal or plant numbers
senses.titleCN: 动植物数量：一个地区的个体量
senses.definition: the number of animals or plants of a kind in a given area, often studied as density or trend
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区某类动植物的个体数量，常以密度或变化趋势来研究
senses.example: The wolf population fell sharply after the hard winter.
senses.exampleCN: 严冬之后狼的数量大幅下降。
senses.why: The counting frame is the key: pick a place and a kind, and the word reports how many are inside it.
senses.whyCN: 关键在于计数框：选定一个地方和一个种类，这个词就报告框里有多少个。

senses.title: The act of settling
senses.titleCN: 迁入定居：使地方有人住（旧义）
senses.definition: the act of filling an area with inhabitants, now mostly expressed by the related verb
senses.definitionCN: 使某地住满居民的行为，现多由相关动词表达
senses.example: The population of the frontier took three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 边疆的移民定居用了三代人的时间。
senses.why: The suffix -ation can name an action as well as a result. This older sense survives in the verb populate and in historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ation 既能命名结果，也能命名动作。这个较旧的义项保留在动词 populate 与历史写作中。

senses.title: A demographic problem
senses.titleCN: 人口结构：政策讨论里的对象
senses.definition: the size and age structure of a society considered as an economic or political issue
senses.definitionCN: 把社会的规模与年龄结构当作经济或政治问题来看待
senses.example: An ageing population puts pressure on pensions and hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 人口老龄化给养老金和医院带来压力。
senses.why: Once governments began counting citizens for policy, population became a problem to be managed, not just a fact to be reported.
senses.whyCN: 当政府开始为政策清点公民，population 就从“被报告的事实”变成“待管理的问题”。

intro.en: Population comes from Latin populus 'the people' through populatio 'a peopling, a laying waste'. The word entered English in the 16th century on the Latin stem populatio(n-).
intro.cn: population 经由拉丁语 populatio“使人居住；蹂躏”上溯到 populus“人民”。16 世纪以拉丁词干 populatio(n-) 进入英语。

items.en: populus meant 'the people' as a body. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it may come from Etruscan, and no reliable Latin root can be given, so the deeper layer should be marked as uncertain in origin.
items.cn: populus 指作为整体的“人民”。其更深来源不确定，可能来自伊特鲁里亚语，无法给出可靠的拉丁词根，因此更深一层应标注“来源不确定”。

items.en: populatio in classical Latin could mean both 'a peopling, settlement' and 'a devastating, laying waste'. The two senses seem to come from two verbs that looked alike.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语中 populatio 既可指“使人定居”，也可指“蹂躏、毁坏”。两个义项似乎来自两个外形相近的动词。

items.en: English takes the word in the 1500s first as 'the peopling of a place', then quickly as 'the number of inhabitants'.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪先取“使地方有人居住”之义，随后很快转为“居民数量”。

items.en: With the growth of censuses in the 18th and 19th centuries, population becomes the standard word for an official count of residents.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪人口普查兴起，population 成为官方居民统计的标准用词。

items.en: In the 20th century biology adopts the word for any interbreeding group, transferring the census idea from citizens to individuals of one species.
items.cn: 20 世纪生物学借用该词指任何能相互繁殖的群体，把人口普查的思路从公民转到同一物种的个体。

items.en: Statistics completes the abstraction: the population is now any complete set from which a sample is drawn.
items.cn: 统计学完成了抽象化：population 现在指任何被抽样的完整集合。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the popul- shape and the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group shares the idea of people or counted individuals but differs in what is being counted.
note.cn: 形近组共享 popul- 外形与同一拉丁词干；近义组都涉及“人”或“被计数的个体”，差别在计数对象。

entries.definition: full of people, densely inhabited. It describes a place, while population names the people or their number.
entries.definitionCN: 人口稠密的；住满人的。它描述地方，而 population 命名人或其数量。

entries.definition: to fill an area with people or animals. It names the act that produces a population.
entries.definitionCN: 居住于；使有人居住。它命名产生 population 的那个动作。

entries.definition: liked by many people. It goes back to populus too, but through the sense 'of the people', not through counting them.
entries.definitionCN: 受欢迎的。它同样上溯到 populus，但走的是“属于人民的”这条义线，而不是计数。

entries.definition: the people who live in a place. It names them directly, while population can mean either the people or their count.
entries.definitionCN: 居民。它直接命名人，而 population 既可指人也可指数量。

entries.definition: people with legal membership in a state. It is a legal category, while population is a demographic count that includes non-citizens.
entries.definitionCN: 公民。它是法律范畴，而 population 是包含非公民的人口统计。

entries.definition: a group linked by shared place or interests. It stresses relationships, while population stresses mere co-presence and number.
entries.definitionCN: 社区；群体。它强调关系，而 population 强调共同在场与数量。

entries.definition: the statistical structure of a population, such as age and income. It analyses a population rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 人口结构。指年龄、收入等统计构成，是对 population 的分析而非命名。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: popul- is the stem of Latin populus 'people', so population and popular sit in the same family.
normal.cn: popul- 是拉丁 populus“人民”的词干，所以 population 与 popular 同属一族。

normal.en: The -ation suffix turns people into a countable quantity, which is why the word collocates with growth, density and decline.
normal.cn: -ation 后缀把“人”变成可计量的量，所以这个词常与增长、密度、下降搭配。

normal.en: population density is arithmetic made visible: people divided by area.
normal.cn: 人口密度就是可视化的算术：人数除以面积。

normal.en: In biology the census frame is kept but the citizens become finches, wolves or trees.
normal.cn: 生物学保留了普查的计数框，只把公民换成了雀鸟、狼或树木。

normal.en: In statistics population is the whole set, and sample is the part taken from it.
normal.cn: 统计学里总体是全集，样本是从中取出的部分。

abstract.en: Picture a map covered with dots, then zoom in until each dot becomes a face.
abstract.cn: 想象一张布满小点的地图，再放大到每个点变成一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a census form that asks one question only: how many of you are there?
abstract.cn: 想象一张只问一个问题的普查表：你们有多少人？

abstract.en: Picture a jar of seeds: the jar is the statistical population, the handful you test is the sample.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐种子：罐子是统计总体，抓出来试的一把是样本。

examples.en: Population growth slowed once the factories closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，人口增长放缓了。

examples.en: The study tracked a population of six hundred patients over five years.
examples.cn: 该研究在五年间追踪了六百名患者组成的人群。

examples.en: Statisticians distinguish the population from the sample drawn out of it.
examples.cn: 统计学家把总体与从中抽取的样本区别开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: “泡皮溜”音近 population：一群人泡在水里、皮都溜滑——人多得像下饺子 → population 人口

root: 拉丁 populus“人民”（更深来源不确定，可能出自伊特鲁里亚语）；populatio(n-) 词干 + -ation 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question with different boundaries: how many are inside this frame?
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题，只是换边界：这个框里有多少？

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map of dots, each dot a person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张由小点构成的地图，每个点是一个人。

branches.en: COUNT AND BODY: the number and the living community are one word seen twice, once as arithmetic and once as society.
branches.cn: 数字与群体：数量与活生生的社区是同一个词的两种看法，一是算术，一是社会。

branches.en: NAMED SUBGROUP: students, patients and workers each get their own population once a boundary is drawn.
branches.cn: 特定人群：一旦画出边界，学生、病人、劳动者各自成一个人群。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN COUNT: breeding groups and wildlife numbers apply the census frame to other species.
branches.cn: 非人类计数：繁殖群体与野生动物数量把普查的框套到其他物种上。

branches.en: STATISTICAL WHOLE: the population is whatever complete set a sample is taken from.
branches.cn: 统计总体：population 就是任何被抽样的完整集合。

branches.en: PROCESS AND POLICY: settling an area and managing an ageing society are the verb side and the political side of the same noun.
branches.cn: 过程与政策：让人定居与管理老龄化社会，是同一名词的动词面与政治面。

intro.en: Population is the Latin stem popul- plus -ation. The suffix marks a result or an action, and the same stem yields the adjective populous and the verb populate.
intro.cn: population 是拉丁词干 popul- 加 -ation。后缀标记结果或动作，同一词干还产出形容词 populous 与动词 populate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family runs from populus 'people' to populatio 'settlement, devastation' and populosus 'full of people'. English keeps popul- throughout.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族从 populus“人民”延伸到 populatio“定居、毁坏”与 populosus“人多的”。英语始终保留 popul-。

items.meaning: to fill a place with inhabitants
items.meaningCN: 居住于；使有人居住（popul-“人民”+ -ate 动词后缀）
items.example: Settlers populated the valley within a decade.
items.exampleCN: 定居者十年内就住满了这个山谷。

items.meaning: the people of an area or a counted group
items.meaningCN: 人口；种群（-ion 构成结果名词）
items.example: The population is estimated at two million.
It is the most populous province in the country.
items.exampleCN: 它是全国人口最多的省份。

items.meaning: the loss of inhabitants from an area
items.example: Rural depopulation has closed many schools.
items.exampleCN: 农村人口流失使许多学校关闭。

items.meaning: too many people for the resources available
items.exampleCN: 人口过剩使供水系统吃紧。

items.meaning: liked or accepted by many people
items.meaningCN: 受欢迎的；大众的（-ar“属于……的”）
items.example: The measure is popular with younger voters.
items.exampleCN: 该措施受年轻选民欢迎。

items.meaning: a politician who appeals to ordinary people
items.meaningCN: 民粹主义者（-ist 指“以人民名义行事者”）
items.example: The populist won by attacking experts.
items.exampleCN: 这位民粹主义者靠攻击专家赢得选举。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 人民；国民（更深来源不确定）

latinEntries.meaning: a peopling, settlement; also a laying waste
the popular party in Roman politics
latinEntries.meaningCN: 平民派（罗马政治中的“人民派”）

definition_zh: 港口；港市；端口；左舷；（把舵）转向左舷；波尔图葡萄酒
definition_en: a harbor where ships load and unload, an opening on a device for a cable, the left side of a ship, a fortified wine from Porto, or to turn a ship to the left
core_image: 码头边一排起重机，一艘货轮把船头缓缓靠向岸壁
scene: 黎明前的海湾里，灯塔还亮着，一艘货轮正慢慢靠上码头。By dawn the cargo ship had entered the port and begun to unload.
sceneCN: 这里 port 是「港口」（第 1 个义项：船只装卸货物的港湾）；句意为天亮时货轮已经进港开始卸货。图中可辨识物件：海湾、灯塔、货轮、码头。

pos.zh: 港口；港市；端口；左舷；波尔图葡萄酒
把舵转向左舷；使船靠左

derivatives.zh: 由 air 与 port（港口、停靠地）复合，义为「机场」
由 sea 与 port 复合，义为「海港；港市」
由拉丁 porta（门）加 -al 构成，义为「门户；入口」
由 port 加 -age 构成，义为「水陆之间的搬运；搬运费」

senses.title: A harbor where ships load and unload
senses.definition: a place on a coast or river where ships can tie up and where goods and passengers are loaded or unloaded
senses.definitionCN: 海岸或河边供船只停靠、装卸货物和上下旅客的地方
senses.example: The fishing boats return to port before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船在暴风雨来临前回到港口。
senses.why: Latin portus named a sheltered place where a ship could lie safely; English borrowed it early, so the first sense is simply that stopping place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 portus 指船只能安全停靠的有遮蔽之处；英语借入得很早，所以第一个义项就是这个停靠点本身。

senses.title: A socket for a cable or device
senses.definition: an opening or socket on a computer or machine where a cable, plug or storage device is connected
senses.definitionCN: 计算机或机器上用来连接线缆、插头或存储设备的开口或插槽
senses.example: Plug the monitor into the port at the back of the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 把显示器插到机器背面的接口上。
senses.why: A port is also a gateway, a sense that came through Latin porta, a door; the socket is the narrow doorway through which signals enter and leave a machine.
senses.whyCN: port 也曾指「门户」，这一支经拉丁语 porta（门）而来；插槽就是信号进出机器的那道窄门。

senses.title: The left side of a ship
senses.definition: the left-hand side of a ship or aircraft when you are facing the front
senses.definitionCN: 面朝船头或机头时，船或飞机的左侧
senses.example: The lighthouse passed along the port side as the ship turned.
senses.exampleCN: 船转向时，灯塔从船的左舷掠过。
senses.why: One common explanation is that ships tied up with their loading side to the quay, so the harbor side became the name for the left; the derivation is still debated.
senses.whyCN: 一种常见解释是，船进港时把装卸的一侧靠向码头，于是「靠港的那一边」成了左舷的名字；这一来源仍有争论。

senses.title: A fortified wine from Porto
senses.definition: a sweet, strong red wine made in the Douro valley and shipped through the city of Porto
senses.definitionCN: 在杜罗河谷酿造、经波尔图城运出的甜型高度红葡萄酒
senses.example: They finished dinner with a glass of port and some cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以一杯波尔图葡萄酒配奶酪结束了晚餐。
senses.why: The drink took its English name from Porto, the Portuguese city at the river mouth, so a place name shrank into a short everyday word.
senses.whyCN: 这种酒的英语名取自河口城市波尔图，于是一个地名缩成了日常使用的短词。

senses.title: To turn a ship to the left
senses.definition: to turn a ship or its helm towards the left side
senses.definitionCN: 把船或船舵转向左侧
senses.example: The captain ported the helm to avoid the drifting buoy.
senses.exampleCN: 船长把舵转向左舷，避开漂来的浮标。
senses.why: Once port names the left side, the verb applies that direction to steering: to port the helm is to send the bow that way.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 port 成为左舷的名称，动词就把这个方向用到操舵上：把舵转向左舷，就是让船头朝那边摆。

intro.en: The short word port joins three Latin threads: portus, a harbor, porta, a gate, and the wine named after the city of Porto.
intro.cn: 这个短词 port 汇合了三条拉丁线索：portus（港口）、porta（门），以及得名于波尔图城的葡萄酒。

items.en: Portus meant a harbor or haven, a sheltered place where a ship could lie safely; it is generally connected with an old root for passing through or crossing.
items.cn: portus 意为港口、避风处，是船只能安全停泊的有遮蔽之处；一般认为它与表示「穿过、越过」的古老词根有关。

items.en: Porta meant a gate or door, and it is the source of port in the sense of an opening, including the socket on a computer.
items.cn: porta 意为大门、出入口；表示「开口」的 port 就来自这里，电脑上的插口也属于这一支。

items.en: English borrowed port for a harbor from Latin, partly through Old French; by the Middle Ages it named both seaports and gateways.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语借来表示港口的 port，其中一部分经古法语传入；到中世纪，它既指海港，也指出入口。

items.en: Port came to name the left side of a ship, usually explained by the side laid against the quay for loading; the explanation is not certain.
items.cn: port 开始指船的左舷，通常解释为进港装卸时靠向码头的那一侧；这一解释并不确定。

items.en: Porto in Portugal gave port wine its name, while computing made port a socket for cables and signals.
items.cn: 葡萄牙的波尔图给了波尔图葡萄酒这个名字，计算机则让 port 成为线缆与信号用的插口。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and relatives of the short form; the near-meaning group gathers words for sheltered water and places where ships tie up.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个短词构成的复合词与同族词；近义组收表示避风水域与船只停靠处的词。

entries.definition: A place where aircraft take off and land, built on port in the old sense of a stopping place.
entries.definitionCN: 由 air 与 port 复合，指飞机起降的机场；这里的 port 保留了「停靠地」的旧义。

entries.definition: A town or city with a harbor used by seagoing ships.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sea 与 port 复合，指拥有海港的城市。

entries.definition: A doorway or entrance, especially a large one; from Latin porta.
entries.definitionCN: 与表示「门」的 port 同出拉丁 porta，义为门户、入口。

entries.definition: Able to be carried; built on Latin portare, a different source from the harbor word.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，但来自拉丁 portare（搬运），与「港口」的 port 不是同一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: A sheltered body of water where ships can stay safely.
entries.definitionCN: 港湾；强调有遮蔽、可避风，与港口近义。

entries.definition: A structure at the water's edge where a ship is loaded, repaired or kept.
entries.definitionCN: 码头；船坞；强调靠岸装卸或修船的具体设施。

entries.definition: A flat platform at a harbor where ships are loaded and unloaded.
entries.definitionCN: 码头；强调沿岸用于装卸的平台。

entries.definition: A small harbor designed for pleasure boats.
entries.definitionCN: 游艇码头；专供休闲船只停泊的小港。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on Latin portus for a harbor, and the same spelling has picked up a gate, a ship's side and a wine along the way.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词立足于表示港口的拉丁语 portus，同一个拼写沿途又接上了门、船舷与一种酒。

normal.en: Port comes from Latin portus, a harbor, and English had the word early enough to use it for any place a ship stops.
normal.cn: port 来自拉丁语 portus（港口），英语借入很早，凡船停靠之处都能用它。

normal.en: A computer port is a gate for signals, which is why this sense goes back to Latin porta, a door, rather than to portus.
normal.cn: 电脑端口是信号进出的门，所以这一义项上溯的是拉丁语 porta（门），而不是 portus。

normal.en: Port side is the left side of a ship; the usual explanation is that the loading side lay against the quay in harbor.
normal.cn: port side 是船的左舷；常见解释是装卸的一侧在港里靠着码头。

normal.en: Port wine is named after Porto, the Portuguese city at the mouth of the Douro.
normal.cn: port wine 得名于杜罗河口的葡萄牙城市波尔图。

normal.en: Airport and seaport stretch port from a harbor to any place where vehicles stop and load.
normal.cn: airport 与 seaport 把 port 从港湾扩展到任何车辆停靠、装卸的地方。

abstract.en: A harbor is where a journey pauses, so one short word can name a ship's rest, a signal's doorway and a glass at the end of dinner.
abstract.cn: 港口是旅程暂停的地方，所以一个短词既能指船的歇脚处，也能指信号的门口和晚餐末尾的一杯酒。

abstract.en: A port is a controlled opening: water, people and data all pass through a narrow gate that can be watched.
abstract.cn: 端口是一道受控的开口：水、人和数据都得从一道可以被看守的窄门通过。

abstract.en: The left side of a ship is named from the shore it once faced, a reminder that directions are often borrowed from land.
abstract.cn: 船的左舷用它曾经面对的岸来命名，这提醒人：方向常常是从陆地借来的。

examples.en: By dawn the cargo ship had entered the port and begun to unload.
examples.cn: 天亮时货轮已经进港开始卸货。

examples.en: Plug the monitor into the port at the back of the machine.
examples.cn: 把显示器插到机器背面的接口上。

examples.en: They finished dinner with a glass of port and some cheese.
examples.cn: 他们以一杯波尔图葡萄酒配奶酪结束了晚餐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「波特」——船停在港湾里卸货，杯里也盛着波尔图来的甜酒；port 就是港口，也是端口、左舷与波尔图酒。

root: port 背后有三条拉丁线：portus（港口、避风处）、porta（门，电脑端口由此而来）与 portare（搬运，portable、porter 由此而来）；三者深层同源，但在拉丁语里是彼此不同的词。port wine 则得名于葡萄牙城市波尔图。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a sheltered place where movement stops; the senses branch into the harbor, the gate for signals, the ship's left side, the wine of Porto and the act of turning that way.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是运动暂停的有遮蔽之处；义项由此分出港口、信号的门、船左舷、波尔图酒，以及朝那边转舵的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cranes along a quay, a freighter easing its bow towards the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：码头边一排起重机，一艘货轮把船头缓缓靠向岸壁。

branches.en: cranes lifting containers beside a docked freighter
branches.cn: 起重机在靠岸的货轮旁吊起集装箱

branches.en: a cable clicking into a socket at the back of a machine
branches.cn: 线缆咔哒一声插进机器背面的插槽

branches.en: a lighthouse sliding past the left rail of a ship
branches.cn: 灯塔从船左侧的栏杆旁滑过

branches.en: a small glass of dark red wine after dinner
branches.cn: 晚餐后一小杯深红色的甜酒

branches.en: a helm turned so the bow swings towards the quay
branches.cn: 船舵转向，让船头朝码头一侧摆去

intro.en: The form is short, but it carries three Latin nouns: a harbor, a gate and a carrying verb that also built portable and porter.
intro.cn: 这个词形很短，却背着三个拉丁名词：港口、门，以及一个也造出了 portable 与 porter 的「搬运」动词。

latinIntro.en: Three Latin words stand behind this short form: portus for a harbor, porta for a gate, and portare for carrying; they are related at a deeper level but were separate words in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个短词背后有三个拉丁词：portus（港口）、porta（门）与 portare（搬运）；它们在更早的层次上相关，但在拉丁语里是彼此独立的词。

items.meaning: air plus port, a place for aircraft
items.meaningCN: 由 air 与 port 复合，指机场

items.meaning: sea plus port, a harbor town
items.meaningCN: 由 sea 与 port 复合，指海港城市

definition_zh: 便携的；可携带的；轻便的；可移植的；便携设备
definition_en: light and small enough to be carried easily, designed for use in different places, able to be moved to another system or job, or a small device that can be carried
core_image: 一台合上盖子就能塞进背包的笔记本电脑，提手上还留着体温
scene: 清晨的候车室里，一名记者把折叠好的小键盘从背包里取出来，放在膝上。She carries a portable keyboard so she can write on the train.
sceneCN: 这里 portable 是「便携的」（第 1 个义项：轻便、容易携带）；句意为她带着一个便携键盘，好在火车上写作。图中可辨识物件：候车室、背包、小键盘。

pos.zh: 便携的；可携带的；轻便的；可移植的
便携设备；便携式器具

derivatives.zh: 由 portable 加 -ity 构成，义为「便携性；可移植性」
由 portable 加 -ly 构成，义为「便携地；可携带地」
由 trans-（穿过）加拉丁 portare（搬运）与 -able 构成，与 portable 共享词根，义为「可运输的」

senses.title: Light enough to be carried
senses.definition: small and light enough that a person can carry it from place to place without difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 体积与重量都小，一个人可以毫不费力地带着它到处走
senses.example: The radio is small and portable enough to fit in a coat pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 这台收音机很小，便携得能放进大衣口袋。
senses.why: Latin portare means to carry and -abilis means able to be, so the adjective starts as a plain claim that an object can be carried.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 portare 意为搬运，-abilis 意为「能够被……」；这个形容词起初只是直说一件东西可以被带着走。

senses.title: Designed to be used on the move
senses.definition: of equipment, built to work in different places rather than fixed in one room or building
senses.definitionCN: 指设备被造得可以在不同地点使用，而不是固定在一间屋子或一栋楼里
senses.example: The clinic uses a portable X-ray machine for home visits.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所用一台便携式 X 光机出诊。
senses.why: Once a machine can be carried, it can also be used where the patient is; the sense shifts from the weight of the object to the freedom of the place it can serve.
senses.whyCN: 一台机器只要能搬动，就能到病人所在的地方使用；义项于是从物体的重量转到它能服务的地点自由。

senses.title: Able to be moved to another system
senses.definition: of software, skills or benefits, able to be moved from one computer system, employer or country to another
senses.definitionCN: 指软件、技能或福利能够从一套计算机系统、一个雇主或一个国家转移到另一个
senses.example: The pension is portable, so workers keep it when they change jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 这份养老金可以转移，所以工人换工作时能把它带走。
senses.why: The carrying image is applied to things that are not physical: a skill or a pension is portable if it travels with the person instead of staying behind.
senses.whyCN: 「搬运」的形象被用到非实物上：一项技能或一份养老金若能跟着人走而不是留在原处，就是 portable。

senses.title: A small device that can be carried
senses.definition: a small machine such as a radio, television or computer that is designed to be carried around
senses.definitionCN: 收音机、电视或电脑之类为随身携带而设计的小型机器
senses.example: He listened to the match on a little portable in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 他在厨房用一台小便携收音机听比赛。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun when the object is obvious from context; the portable is simply the portable set.
senses.whyCN: 当所指物品在语境里已经很明显，英语常把形容词直接当名词用；the portable 就是「那台便携的机器」。

intro.en: Portable is Latin portare, to carry, plus the suffix -abilis, able to be; it reached English through Old French as a plain adjective for things easy to move.
intro.cn: portable 是拉丁语 portare（搬运）加上后缀 -abilis（能够被……）构成的，经古法语进入英语，最初只是形容容易搬动的东西。

items.en: Portare is the Latin verb for carrying, and it also stands behind porter, transport and import.
items.cn: portare 是拉丁语中表示搬运的动词，porter、transport、import 也都出自它。

items.en: The suffix -abilis marked what can be done to something, as in the modern English -able.
items.cn: 后缀 -abilis 表示「可以被……的」，相当于现代英语的 -able。

items.en: Portabilis joined the two: an object that can be carried, with no suggestion yet of electronics or jobs.
items.cn: portabilis 把两者合起来，指可以被携带的物体，那时还没有电子产品或职业的含义。

items.en: Old French kept the adjective as portable, and English borrowed it in the late Middle Ages for furniture and small goods that could be moved.
items.cn: 古法语保留了这个形容词 portable，英语在中世纪后期借入，用来形容可以搬动的家具与小件物品。

items.en: Modern English applies it to radios, computers, pensions and software, so the word now measures how easily something travels with its owner.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用在收音机、电脑、养老金与软件上，于是这个词衡量的是某物能多方便地跟着主人走。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers family forms and the harbor word port; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for things easy to move or hold.
note.cn: 形近组收同族形式以及表示港口的 port；近义组收形容容易移动或持握之物的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being easy to carry or move to another system.
entries.definitionCN: 由 portable 加 -ity 构成，义为「便携性；可移植性」。

entries.definition: A harbor or an opening for a cable; this word comes from Latin portus, not from portare.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，但表示港口的 port 来自拉丁 portus，与 portable 的搬运词根不同。

entries.definition: A person who carries luggage, built on the same Latin verb portare.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一拉丁动词 portare 构成，指替人搬运行李的人。

entries.definition: Able to be transported; the same carrying verb with the prefix trans-.
entries.definitionCN: 由 trans-（穿过）加同一搬运词根与 -able 构成，义为「可运输的」。

entries.definition: Able to move or be moved easily.
entries.definitionCN: 可移动的；强调能移动，不强调能随身携带。

entries.definition: Small and neatly fitted into little space.
entries.definitionCN: 紧凑的；强调体积小、占空间少。

entries.definition: Small enough to be held and used in the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 手持的；强调用手握住使用。

entries.definition: Weighing less than usual and therefore easy to move.
entries.definitionCN: 轻量的；强调重量轻。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin verb for carrying plus a suffix of possibility, and its family keeps returning to light objects that travel with their owner.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「搬运」动词加上表示可能性的后缀，同族词反复回到能跟着主人走动的轻便物件。

normal.en: Portable is portare plus -abilis, so its oldest meaning is simply able to be carried.
normal.cn: portable 是 portare 加 -abilis，所以它最古老的意思就是「可以被搬运的」。

normal.en: Porter takes the same verb and adds -er for the person; portable describes the thing, porter the one who carries it.
normal.cn: porter 用同一个动词加 -er 指人；portable 形容东西，porter 指搬东西的人。

normal.en: Portability adds -ity to portable and names the quality, which is why portable software can run on more than one system.
normal.cn: portability 在 portable 后加 -ity，指这种性质，所以 portable software 能在不止一套系统上运行。

normal.en: A portable pension or a portable skill travels with the worker instead of staying with one employer.
normal.cn: 可转移的养老金或可迁移的技能会跟着工人走，而不是留在某一位雇主那里。

normal.en: Transportable adds trans-, across, to the same carrying root, so it means able to be carried from place to place.
normal.cn: transportable 在同一搬运词根前加 trans-（穿过），意为可以从一处运到另一处。

abstract.en: Portable things are not merely light; their usefulness travels with them.
abstract.cn: 便携之物不只是轻，它们的好处能跟着人一起移动。

abstract.en: A skill is portable when no single employer owns it, which is why the word moved from radios to careers.
abstract.cn: 一项技能若不属于某一位雇主，就是可转移的；这也解释了这个词为何从收音机走到了职业。

abstract.en: Anything portable asks for a smaller form, not a smaller purpose.
abstract.cn: 任何便携之物要求的是更小的形体，而不是更小的用途。

examples.en: She carries a portable keyboard so she can write on the train.
examples.cn: 她带着一个便携键盘，好在火车上写作。

examples.en: The pension is portable, so workers keep it when they change jobs.
examples.cn: 这份养老金可以转移，所以工人换工作时能把它带走。

examples.en: The clinic uses a portable X-ray machine for home visits.
examples.cn: 这家诊所用一台便携式 X 光机出诊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡特薄」——薄薄一台，提起来就能走；portable 就是便携的、可携带的。

root: 由拉丁 portare（搬运）加 -abilis（能……的）构成，经古法语 portable 进入英语；与 porter（搬运工）、transport（运输）同出一源。注意与来自 portus（港口）的 port 区分：拼写相近，拉丁来源不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an object that can be carried; the senses divide into its lightness, its use on the move, its transfer to other systems, and the device itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是可以被带着走的物件；义项由此分出轻便、可在移动中使用、可转移到别的系统，以及这种设备本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a laptop closing into a backpack, its handle still warm from the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台合上盖子就能塞进背包的笔记本电脑，提手上还留着体温。

branches.en: a radio slipping into a coat pocket
branches.cn: 收音机塞进大衣口袋

branches.en: an X-ray machine wheeled into a patient's home
branches.cn: X 光机被推进病人家中

branches.en: a pension account moving to a new employer
branches.cn: 养老金账户转到新雇主名下

branches.en: a small radio playing on a kitchen shelf
branches.cn: 厨房搁板上响着的小收音机

branches.en: skills that travel with a worker from job to job
branches.cn: 随工人换工作而迁移的技能

intro.en: The adjective is built from the Latin verb for carrying and a suffix of possibility, and the same pieces also build porter, portability and transportable.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由拉丁语「搬运」动词与表示可能性的后缀构成，同样的部件还造出了 porter、portability 与 transportable。

latinIntro.en: Portable goes back to the Latin verb portare, to carry, and the adjective portabilis, able to be carried; the family is Latin rather than Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: portable 上溯拉丁动词 portare（搬运）与形容词 portabilis（可携带的）；这个词族属于拉丁语而非日耳曼语。

items.meaning: able to be carried or moved

definition_zh: 搬运工；行李员；医院勤杂工；门房；看门人；黑啤酒
definition_en: a person paid to carry luggage, a hospital worker who moves patients and equipment, a doorkeeper or caretaker, or a dark beer
core_image: 车站月台上，一个穿制服的人把两只旧皮箱一前一后提在手里
scene: 深夜的旅馆门口，雨还在下，一个穿制服的人接过旅客手里的两只大箱子。The porter carried both suitcases up the narrow stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 porter 是「搬运工、行李员」（第 1 个义项：替人搬运行李的人）；句意为行李员把两只箱子搬上窄楼梯。图中可辨识物件：旅馆门口、雨、大箱子、制服。

pos.zh: 搬运工；行李员；医院勤杂工；门房；看门人；黑啤酒

derivatives.zh: 由 porter 加 -age 构成，义为「搬运；搬运费」
由 porter 与 house 复合，原指兼卖黑啤酒的餐馆，后指一种厚切牛排
由 porter 加 -ess 构成，义为「女门房；女搬运工」

senses.title: A person paid to carry luggage
senses.definition: a person whose job is to carry bags and luggage for travellers, especially at a station or hotel
senses.definitionCN: 以替旅客搬运行李为职业的人，尤指在车站或旅馆工作的人
senses.example: The porter carried both suitcases up the narrow stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 行李员把两只箱子搬上窄楼梯。
senses.why: Latin portare means to carry and -er names the person who does it; the first sense is simply the carrying job.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 portare 意为搬运，-er 指做这件事的人；第一个义项就是这份搬运的工作。

senses.title: A hospital worker who moves patients
senses.definition: a hospital worker who moves patients, beds, samples or equipment between wards
senses.definitionCN: 在医院各病房之间运送病人、病床、样本或设备的勤杂人员
senses.example: A porter wheeled her down to the X-ray department.
senses.exampleCN: 一名勤杂工用轮椅把她推到放射科。
senses.why: Hospitals borrowed the carrying word for the staff who move people and equipment, because the job is still transport inside a building.
senses.whyCN: 医院借用了这个「搬运」词来称运送人与设备的员工，因为这份工作仍是在楼内做运输。

senses.title: A doorkeeper or caretaker
senses.definition: a person who guards the entrance of a building, especially a college or a block of flats, and often looks after it
senses.definitionCN: 看守建筑物入口的人，尤指学院或公寓楼的看门人，往往还兼管杂务
senses.example: The porter at the college gate checked our names before letting us in.
senses.exampleCN: 学院门口的门房先核对了我们的名字才放行。
senses.why: This sense has a different Latin source: porta means gate, and portarius was the gatekeeper, so one English spelling carries two histories.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项另有拉丁来源：porta 意为门，portarius 是守门人；所以同一个英语拼写背着两段历史。

senses.title: A dark, strong beer
senses.definition: a dark brown beer made with roasted malt, originally associated with London market porters
senses.definitionCN: 用烘烤麦芽酿成的深褐色啤酒，最初与伦敦市场的搬运工有关
senses.example: He ordered a pint of porter and sat by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一品脱黑啤酒，坐到窗边。
senses.why: The drink was shortened from porter's ale, the beer sold to market porters, so the job name became the name of what they drank.
senses.whyCN: 这种酒由 porter's ale 缩略而来，本是卖给市场搬运工的啤酒；于是职业名变成了他们所喝之物的名字。

intro.en: Porter is two Latin words that fell into one English spelling: portare, to carry, and porta, a gate, each with its own Old French descendant.
intro.cn: porter 是两个拉丁词落进同一个英语拼写：portare（搬运）与 porta（门），各自带着自己的古法语后裔。

items.en: Portare meant to carry, and with the agent suffix -arius it gave portarius, a carrier.
items.cn: portare 意为搬运，加上表示施动者的后缀 -arius，就得到 portarius（搬运者）。

items.en: Porta meant a gate or door; the same -arius made portarius a gatekeeper, so the two jobs shared a Latin shape.
items.cn: porta 意为大门、出入口；同一个 -arius 又造出表示守门人的 portarius，两种职业在拉丁语里形状相同。

items.en: Old French carried the two words onward as porteo(u)r, a carrier, and portier, a doorkeeper.
items.cn: 古法语把这两个词分别传成 porteo(u)r（搬运者）与 portier（守门人）。

items.en: Middle English spelled both as porter, so the carrier and the gatekeeper became one form in English.
items.cn: 中古英语把两者都写作 porter，搬运者与守门人由此在英语里合成一个形式。

items.en: Porter beer is short for porter's ale, named for the market porters who drank it; the drink sense is the newest branch.
items.cn: porter 啤酒是 porter's ale 的缩略，得名于喝这种酒的市场搬运工；酒这一义项是最晚长出的分支。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same carrying root and the harbor word; the near-meaning group gathers people who carry or guard entrances.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一「搬运」词根上的形式以及表示港口的词；近义组收搬运东西或看守入口的人。

entries.definition: The work of carrying goods, or the charge for it.
entries.definitionCN: 由 porter 加 -age 构成，义为「搬运工作；搬运费」。

entries.definition: Able to be carried, built on the same Latin verb portare.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一拉丁动词 portare 构成，义为「便携的」。

entries.definition: A harbor or an opening; the harbor word comes from Latin portus, not from the carrying verb.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，但表示港口的 port 来自拉丁 portus，不是搬运词根。

entries.definition: To bring goods into a country, built on portare with the prefix in-.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-（进入）加 portare（搬运）构成，义为「进口」。

entries.definition: A person or company that carries goods or people.
entries.definitionCN: 搬运者；承运人；强调承担运输的人或公司。

entries.definition: A person who carries something, especially in a formal role.
entries.definitionCN: 持送者；强调正式地拿着或递送某物的人。

entries.definition: A person employed to guard the entrance of a building.
entries.definitionCN: 门童；门卫；强调守在门口的人。

entries.definition: A hotel employee who helps guests with luggage, bookings and local information.
entries.definitionCN: 旅馆礼宾员；除行李外还替客人安排事务。

normalIntro.en: The word has two Latin roots, carrying and gatekeeping, and its family keeps returning to loads, entrances and the people who handle them.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词有两条拉丁根，一条是搬运，一条是守门；同族词反复回到货物、入口以及照管它们的人。

normal.en: Porter the carrier is portare plus -er, the person who carries.
normal.cn: 表示搬运工的 porter 是 portare 加 -er，即「搬运的人」。

normal.en: Porter the doorkeeper is porta plus -arius, the person at the gate; the two Latin words became one English spelling.
normal.cn: 表示门房的 porter 是 porta 加 -arius，即「守在门口的人」；两个拉丁词在英语里拼成了同一个样子。

normal.en: Old French porteur meant carrier and portier meant doorkeeper, and English merged them both into porter.
normal.cn: 古法语 porteur 指搬运者，portier 指守门人，英语把两者都并进了 porter。

normal.en: Porter beer was shortened from porter's ale, the dark beer sold to London market porters.
normal.cn: porter 啤酒由 porter's ale 缩略而来，是卖给伦敦市场搬运工的深色啤酒。

normal.en: A hospital porter still carries people rather than bags, which shows how far the carrying sense can stretch.
normal.cn: 医院勤杂工搬的是人而不是行李，可见「搬运」这一义项能伸到多远。

abstract.en: Two jobs share one spelling because a gate and a load both sit at the edge of a journey.
abstract.cn: 两种职业共用一个拼写，因为门与行李都处在旅程的边缘。

abstract.en: A porter stands where arrival becomes entry: he takes the bag or checks the name before the guest goes in.
abstract.cn: 门房站在「到达」变成「进入」的地方：他接过箱子，或先核对名字，客人才能进去。

abstract.en: The beer kept the name of the workers who drank it, which is how a job can outlive itself in a glass.
abstract.cn: 这种酒留下了喝它的工人的名字，一份职业就这样在杯子里延续下来。

examples.en: The porter carried both suitcases up the narrow stairs.
examples.cn: 行李员把两只箱子搬上窄楼梯。

examples.en: A porter wheeled her down to the X-ray department.
examples.cn: 一名勤杂工用轮椅把她推到放射科。

examples.en: He ordered a pint of porter and sat by the window.
examples.cn: 他点了一品脱黑啤酒，坐到窗边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡特」——在坡道上替人提箱子的人；porter 就是搬运工，也是门房。

root: porter 有两条拉丁来路：一条是 portare（搬运）加 -er，指搬运工、行李员；另一条是 porta（门）加 -arius，指门房、看门人。两词在英语里拼成同一个样子。黑啤酒 porter 则由 porter's ale 缩略而来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is someone who handles what passes through a threshold; the senses divide into carrying luggage, moving patients, guarding a gate, and the beer named after carriers.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是照管通过某道门槛之物的人；义项由此分出搬行李、运病人、守大门，以及以搬运工命名的啤酒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a uniformed figure on a station platform holding two old suitcases, one in each hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：车站月台上，一个穿制服的人一前一后提着两只旧皮箱。

branches.en: a bag lifted from a taxi to a hotel desk
branches.cn: 行李从出租车提到旅馆前台

branches.en: a wheelchair pushed along a hospital corridor
branches.cn: 轮椅沿医院走廊被推着

branches.en: a name checked at a college gate
branches.cn: 学院门口核对的姓名

branches.en: a dark pint set down on a pub table
branches.cn: 一杯深色啤酒放到酒馆桌上

branches.en: a uniformed worker standing where people arrive and ask for help
branches.cn: 穿制服的人站在人们到达并求助的地方

intro.en: The word joins a carrying verb and a gate noun to two agent suffixes, and the same pieces also build porterage and the compound porterhouse.
intro.cn: 这个词把「搬运」动词与「门」名词分别接到两个施动后缀上，同样的部件还造出了 porterage 与复合词 porterhouse。

latinIntro.en: Porter comes from two Latin nouns of agency: portarius, a carrier from portare, and portarius, a gatekeeper from porta; Old French kept them apart before English merged the spellings.
latinIntro.cn: porter 来自两个表示施动者的拉丁名词：由 portare 来的「搬运者」，与由 porta 来的「守门人」；古法语还分得清，英语却把拼写合并了。

items.meaning: the work or charge of carrying

definition_zh: 部分；一份（食物）；应得的份额；命运；（动词）分配
definition_en: a part or share of something larger; an amount of food served to one person; to divide something into shares
core_image: 把一整块切开，把属于你的那一份放到你面前
scene: 每位客人都分到了满满一份烤肉。Each guest received a generous portion of the roast.
sceneCN: 这里 portion 是「分给一个人的一份食物」（第 2 个义项：一份）；句意：每位客人都分到了一份量很足的烤肉。场景要点：整块被切开、按人分、放在各自盘里；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 部分；一份；份额；命运
分配；把……分成份

collocations.zh: 最大的一份（源自狮子分猎物的典故）

derivatives.zh: 分摊；按比例分配
比例；均衡（pro- + portion）
成比例的
没有份额的；无嫁妆的（古）

senses.title: A part of a whole
senses.definition: a part of a larger whole, especially one separated or regarded separately
senses.definitionCN: 一个更大整体中的一部分，尤指被分开或单独看待的那部分
senses.example: A large portion of the budget goes to salaries.
senses.exampleCN: 预算中很大一部分用于工资。
senses.why: Latin portio meant a share assigned to someone. The word begins with the act of cutting a whole and handing out pieces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 portio 意为“分派给某人的一份”。这个词起于这样一个动作：把整体切开，再把块分出去。

senses.title: A serving of food
senses.titleCN: 一份（食物）：放到你盘里的量
senses.definition: the amount of food served to one person at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次盛给一个人的食物量
senses.example: Each guest received a generous portion of the roast.
senses.exampleCN: 每位客人都分到了一份量很足的烤肉。
senses.why: Food is the most everyday whole that gets divided. The share on your plate is a portion in the most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 食物是最日常的被分割的整体。你盘里的那一份，就是最具体的 portion。

senses.title: An allotted share of property
senses.titleCN: 应得份额：法律上分给你的那一份
senses.definition: the share of an estate or property that is assigned to a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 遗产或财产中分配给某个特定人的份额
senses.example: She received her portion of the family land at twenty-one.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十一岁时得到了属于自己的那份家族土地。
senses.why: Inheritance makes the metaphor legal: the whole is fixed, the shares are named, and each heir gets a portion.
senses.whyCN: 继承把这个比喻法律化了：整体是固定的，份额是有名分的，每个继承人各得一份。

senses.title: One's lot or fate
senses.titleCN: 命运：分给一生的那一份
senses.definition: the share of life, good or bad, that a person is given, in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 文学用语，指一个人被分得的那一份人生，无论好坏
senses.example: He accepted his portion of suffering without complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫无怨言地接受了分给自己的那份苦难。
senses.why: If goods can be allotted, so can experiences. Life itself becomes a whole divided among people, and yours is your portion.
senses.whyCN: 如果财物可以被分派，经历也可以。人生本身成了一个分给众人的整体，你的那一份就是你的 portion。

senses.title: To divide into shares
senses.definition: to divide something into shares and give them out
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成若干份并发给各人
senses.example: The committee portioned the funds among the three projects.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会把资金分给了三个项目。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act that produced it: to portion is to perform the cutting and handing out.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成产生它的那个动作：to portion 就是执行“切开并分发”这件事。

senses.title: To provide with a dowry
senses.titleCN: 给嫁妆：旧时按份给女儿财产
senses.definition: in older usage, to give a daughter a dowry or a share of property at marriage
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指在女儿出嫁时给她嫁妆或一份财产
senses.example: The will portioned his daughters before his sons.
senses.exampleCN: 遗嘱先给女儿们分好了嫁妆，然后才轮到儿子。
senses.why: A dowry is literally a daughter's portion, the share set aside for her. The verb records that legal practice.
senses.whyCN: 嫁妆字面就是“女儿的那一份”，即为她单留出来的份额。动词记录的就是这一法律习俗。

senses.title: A section of a larger work
senses.titleCN: 章节：一部作品里的一段
senses.definition: one section of a book, document, or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 书、文件或乐曲中的一个段落
senses.example: Only a small portion of the report deals with costs.
senses.exampleCN: 报告里只有一小部分谈到成本。
senses.why: A text is a whole too. It can be divided into sections, and each section is a portion of the text.
senses.whyCN: 文本也是一个整体，可以被分成段落，每一段就是文本的一个 portion。

senses.title: An allocated amount
senses.titleCN: 配额：按规定量给你的数
senses.definition: a measured amount of something allocated to a person or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 按定量分配给某人或某用途的一份数量
senses.example: The daily portion of grain was weighed out at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 每天那份谷物在黎明时称好分出。
senses.why: When the share is measured rather than simply cut, portion means a fixed quantity: a ration by another name.
senses.whyCN: 当份额是被量出来的而不只是切出来的，portion 就指一个固定数量：换个名字的配给量。

intro.en: Portion comes from a Latin word for an assigned share. The step before it rests on a reconstructed form, so that link is probable rather than directly recorded.
intro.cn: portion 来自拉丁语中表示“分派的份额”的词。它前面的一步建立在重构形式上，因此那一环是“很可能”，而非有直接文献记录。

items.en: Portio meant 'a share, a part, an allotted portion'. It is recorded in classical Latin for shares of property and of food.
items.cn: portio 意为“份额、部分、分得的一份”。古典拉丁语中已用它指财产与食物的份额。

items.en: Portio is generally traced to a reconstructed *partio 'division', related to pars 'part' and ultimately to PIE *pere- (2) 'to grant, allot'. The asterisk marks a form found in no text, so this link is probable rather than documented.
items.cn: portio 一般被追溯到重构形式 *partio“划分”，与 pars“部分”相关，并可再上溯到原始印欧语 *pere- (2)“分配、给予”。星号表示这个形式不见于任何文献，所以这一环是“很可能”，而非有据可查。

items.en: Old French took the Latin accusative portionem and shaped it as porcion, meaning a share or a part.
items.cn: 古法语取拉丁语宾格 portionem，改造为 porcion，意为一份或一部分。

items.en: English borrowed porcion in the early 14th century. Early uses are legal and religious: a share of an estate, a share of goods, an assigned lot in life.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪初借入 porcion。早期用法多属法律与宗教：遗产的一份、财物的一份、被分得的人生际遇。

items.en: The everyday sense 'amount of food for one person' develops later and becomes dominant in modern usage, especially in restaurants and diet advice.
items.cn: “一人份食物量”这一日常义发展较晚，却在现代用法中占据主导，尤其在餐饮与饮食建议里。

items.en: The verb appears alongside the noun, and compounds such as apportion and proportion extend the family. All of them keep the picture of cutting a whole into shares.
items.cn: 动词与名词并行出现，apportion、proportion 等复合词扩展了这个词族。它们都保留了“把整体切成份”的画面。

note.en: The first group is built by adding prefixes to portion itself. The second group collects words for parts and shares.
note.cn: 第一组是在 portion 本身前面加前缀构成。第二组收表示“部分与份额”的词。

entries.definition: to divide and assign in due shares. Ad- 'to' plus portion: to give each their portion.
entries.definitionCN: 按应得的份额划分并分配。ad-“向”加 portion：给每个人应得的那一份。

entries.definition: a relation between parts, or a balanced share. Pro- 'in relation to' plus portion gives the idea of shares measured against each other.
entries.definitionCN: 部分之间的关系，或均衡的份额。pro-“相对”加 portion，给出“份额互相比量”的意思。

entries.definition: changing in a fixed ratio with something else. It extends proportion with -al.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一事物按固定比率变化的。它由 proportion 加 -al 扩展而来。

entries.definition: having no share, especially no dowry. Portion plus -less, common in older legal and literary texts.
entries.definitionCN: 没有份额的，尤指没有嫁妆。portion 加 -less，多见于较早的法律与文学文本。

entries.definition: a piece of a whole. Part is the broad neutral word; portion adds the idea of a share assigned to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一块。part 是宽泛中性的词；portion 多出“分配给某人的份额”之意。

entries.definition: a part belonging to or owed to a person. Share matches portion in legal and financial contexts and is more common there.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某人或应归某人的一部分。share 在法律与财务语境中与 portion 相当，且更常用。

entries.definition: an amount of food for one person. Serving is the everyday restaurant word; portion also carries the sense of an allotted share.
entries.definitionCN: 供一个人吃的食物量。serving 是餐馆日常用语；portion 还带有“分得的份额”之意。

entries.definition: an amount officially given out. Allotment stresses official distribution; portion can be informal or literary.
entries.definitionCN: 官方分发的数量。allotment 强调官方分配；portion 可以是非正式的或文学性的。

entries.definition: a fixed allowance of something scarce. Ration implies shortage and control; portion does not.
entries.definitionCN: 对稀缺物资的固定配给量。ration 含短缺与管制之意；portion 不含。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the slice on the plate, the inheritance, the measured grain, the prefix family, and the fate you are dealt.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：盘里的那一块、遗产里的那一份、量出来的谷物、前缀家族、分给你的一生。

normal.en: Picture a whole roast cut into slices. The slice on your plate is your portion.
normal.cn: 想象一整块烤肉被切成片。你盘里的那一片就是你的 portion。

normal.en: Portion out means hand each person their slice, one by one.
normal.cn: portion out 就是一片一片地把属于各人的那份递过去。

normal.en: In a will, the whole estate is divided and each child gets a portion.
normal.cn: 遗嘱里，整份遗产被切开，每个孩子得到一份 portion。

normal.en: A portion of grain weighed at dawn is a ration under another name.
normal.cn: 黎明时称出的那份谷物，就是换个名字的配给量。

normal.en: Apportion, proportion, portionless: same core, different prefixes and suffixes.
normal.cn: apportion、proportion、portionless：同一个核心，不同的前后缀。

abstract.en: Every whole can be cut, and every cut produces an owner; portion is the word where division becomes possession.
abstract.cn: 每个整体都可被切开，每次切开都产生一个所有者；portion 正是“分割变成占有”的那个词。

abstract.en: A portion is a boundary drawn inside a thing, and boundaries are always drawn by someone.
abstract.cn: 一份是在事物内部画出的一条界线，而界线总是由某个人画的。

abstract.en: When life is called a portion, the metaphor admits that not everything is available to everyone.
abstract.cn: 当人生被称为一份 portion 时，这个比喻承认了：并非所有东西对所有人都是可得的。

examples.en: Only a small portion of the manuscript has survived.
examples.cn: 这份手稿只有一小部分留存下来。

examples.en: Restaurants here are known for generous portions at low prices.
examples.cn: 这里的餐馆以分量足、价格低闻名。

examples.en: The land was portioned among the villagers after the reform.
examples.cn: 改革之后，土地被分给了村民。

dict_mnemonic.text: “剖心”——把整颗心剖开，分给每人一份，就是 portion（份额）；注意这只是谐音，与词源无关

root: 拉丁语 portio“份额、部分”（一般追溯到重构形式 *partio“划分”，与 pars“部分”相关，来自 PIE *pere- (2)“分配”）→ 古法语 porcion → 英语 portion（14 世纪初）。

sensesIntro.en: The word always involves cutting a whole and assigning a piece. Food, inheritance, text, and even fate are all wholes of different kinds, and the piece assigned to you is your portion. The verb simply performs that cut.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终涉及“把整体切开并指派一块”。食物、遗产、文本乃至命运，都是不同种类的整体，分给你的那一块就是你的 portion。动词则是执行这一刀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole loaf cut at the table, one slice placed before each person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整条面包在桌上被切开，每个面前放上一片。

chain: A PART CUT FROM A WHOLE

branches.en: PART: a piece of any whole, whether a budget or a book.
branches.cn: 部分：任何整体中的一块，无论是预算还是书。

branches.en: MEASURE: the plate and the scale, food and fixed allowance.
branches.cn: 量：盘子与秤，食物与定量。

branches.en: LAW: inheritance shares and the dowry set aside for a daughter.
branches.cn: 法律：继承份额与为女儿单留的嫁妆。

branches.en: FATE: the share of life dealt to a person.
branches.cn: 命运：分给一个人的那份人生。

branches.en: ACTION: the act of cutting and handing out.
branches.cn: 动作：切开并分发的行为。

intro.en: Portion has generated a small family through prefixes that specify direction or relation (to, for, in ratio) and suffixes that make adjectives and verbs.
intro.cn: portion 通过表示方向或关系的前缀（向、为、按比例）以及构成形容词与动词的后缀，衍生出一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun portio and its related verb forms supplied the base; English built the rest with native endings.
