latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 portio 及其相关动词形式提供了基底；其余部分由英语用本土词尾构造。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 分配者（苏格兰法律用语）

items.meaningCN: 部分（与 portio 关系未证实）

definition_zh: 肖像；画像；人像照片；人物描绘
definition_en: a painting, drawing or photograph of a person, especially of the face, or a description that captures someone's character
core_image: 一张脸被固定在一个姿势里，眼神却继续朝外看
scene: 摄影棚里，摄影师请她略微转头，让光落在颧骨上。The photographer asked her to turn slightly so the portrait caught the light.
sceneCN: 这里 portrait 指「人像照片」（第 2 个义项：以相机拍摄的人物肖像）；句意为摄影师请她略微转头，好让这张人像接住光；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 肖像；画像；人像照片；文字描绘；（纸张的）竖幅

derivatives.zh: portray + -al（名词后缀）→ 描绘出的形象；从「再现动作」转到「产出的形象」
portrait + -ist（从业者）→ 肖像画家；从「作品」转到「作者」
portrait + -ure（行为或结果）→ 肖像画艺术；从「单件」转到「整个实践」
self- + portrait → 自画像；从「他人肖像」转到「自我再现」

senses.title: A painted or drawn image of a person
senses.definition: a painting or drawing representing a person, especially the face
senses.definitionCN: 表现一个人、尤以面部为主的绘画或素描
senses.example: The portrait shows a merchant holding a letter.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像画着一位手持信件的商人。
senses.why: Portrait began as a noun from the verb 'to draw forth'; the drawn likeness of a person is the core that all other senses extend.
senses.whyCN: portrait 最初是动词「拉出、描绘」的名词化；一个人的被描绘形象是其余义项所扩展的核心。

senses.title: A photographic likeness
senses.definition: a photograph of a person, usually posed and framed
senses.definitionCN: 通常经过摆拍与取景的人物照片
senses.example: The photographer asked her to turn slightly so the portrait caught the light.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师请她略微转头，好让这张人像接住光。
senses.why: When photography arrived, the old word for a drawn likeness transferred to the camera: the medium changed, the social function did not.
senses.whyCN: 摄影出现后，旧有的「绘制形象」一词转到相机上：媒介变了，社会功能没变。

senses.title: A description in words
senses.definition: a literary description that captures a person's appearance and character
senses.definitionCN: 在文学中捕捉一个人外貌与性格的描写
senses.example: The novel opens with a portrait of the aunt at her piano.
senses.exampleCN: 小说开篇是姑妈坐在钢琴前的一幅文字肖像。
senses.why: The metaphor 'portrait in words' treats language as a surface that can hold a likeness, an extension recorded in the eighteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 「文字中的肖像」这一隐喻把语言当作能承载形象的表面，这一扩展在 18 世纪有记录。

senses.title: A filmic depiction of a place or group
senses.titleCN: 影视对地点或群体的描绘
senses.definition: a film or television work that depicts a place, community or period in depth
senses.definitionCN: 深入描绘一个地点、群体或时期的电影或电视作品
senses.example: The documentary is a portrait of a fishing town in decline.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片是一个衰落渔港的肖像。
senses.why: The sense widens from a person to any subject treated as a character: a place can be given a face by a film.
senses.whyCN: 词义从人扩展到任何被当作角色处理的对象：一部影片可以给一个地方一张脸。

senses.title: The genre in art history
senses.titleCN: 艺术史中的肖像画门类
senses.definition: the genre of portraiture as classified in art history
senses.definitionCN: 艺术史分类中的肖像画门类
senses.example: Portrait was ranked below history painting in the academy.
senses.exampleCN: 在学院体系里，肖像画的等级低于历史画。
senses.why: A kind of work becomes a genre, so the noun can name the category rather than one object.
senses.whyCN: 一类作品会变成一个门类，因此这个名词能命名类别，而非单件作品。

senses.title: A likeness in any medium
senses.titleCN: 任何媒介中的相似形象
senses.definition: a representation of a person's appearance in any medium
senses.definitionCN: 在任何媒介中对一个人外貌的再现
senses.example: The coin bears a portrait in low relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚钱币上有浅浮雕肖像。
senses.why: Once the word means 'likeness', the material is free: paint, stone, metal and pixels can all carry a portrait.
senses.whyCN: 一旦词义是「相似形象」，材料就不受限制：颜料、石头、金属与像素都能承载肖像。

senses.title: Vertical page or screen format
senses.definition: the upright orientation of a page, photograph or screen
senses.definitionCN: 页面、照片或屏幕的竖直方向
senses.example: Switch the page to portrait before printing.
senses.exampleCN: 打印前把页面改成竖幅。
senses.why: A portrait painting is typically taller than it is wide, so the format inherited the name of its usual subject.
senses.whyCN: 肖像画通常高大于宽，因此这种版式继承了其常见题材的名称。

senses.title: A sculpted head or bust
senses.definition: a sculpted head or bust representing a person
senses.definitionCN: 表现一个人的雕塑头部或胸像
senses.example: A marble portrait of the founder stands in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 一尊创始人的大理石胸像立在大厅里。
senses.why: Sculpture adopts the word because the aim is still a recognisable person, even when the medium is stone rather than paint.
senses.whyCN: 雕塑采用这个词，因为目标仍是可辨认的个人，即使媒介是石头而非颜料。

intro.en: Portrait came into English in the sixteenth century from French, ultimately from Latin protrahere 'to draw forth'; it is a doublet of portray. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: portrait 于 16 世纪从法语进入英语，最终来自拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」；它与 portray 是同源双重词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Protrahere meant 'to draw forth, drag out, reveal'; it joined pro- 'forth' to trahere 'to draw, drag'.
items.cn: protrahere 意为「拉出、拖出、显露」，由 pro-「向前」与 trahere「拉、拖」组合。

items.en: Old French portraire meant 'to draw, paint, portray', literally 'to trace forth'; medieval Latin also used protrahere for painting.
items.cn: 古法语 portraire 意为「画、描绘」，字面是「向前描出」；中世纪拉丁也用 protrahere 指绘画。

items.en: Old French portret, the past participle of portraire used as a noun, named a drawn or painted figure.
items.cn: 古法语 portret 是 portraire 的过去分词名词化，指被绘制的人物形象。

items.en: English portrait is recorded in the 1560s as 'a figure drawn or painted', a back-formation from portraiture or a direct borrowing from French.
items.cn: 英语 portrait 于 16 世纪 60 年代有记录，指「被绘制的人物形象」，或由 portraiture 逆构，或直接借自法语。

items.en: The sense narrowed to the head and face represented from life, which became the central everyday meaning.
items.cn: 词义收窄到写生表现的头部与面部，这成为日常核心义。

items.en: Photography, film and printing extended the word to camera likenesses, depictions of places and vertical page formats.
items.cn: 摄影、电影与印刷把这个词扩展到相机拍摄的肖像、地点描绘与竖幅版式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words that are constantly confused with portrait; group two holds nouns for likenesses that differ in medium or scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、常与 portrait 混淆的词；第二组是不同媒介或范围的人物再现名词。

entries.definition: The art of making portraits, or portraits collectively; portrait is one work.
entries.definitionCN: 制作肖像的艺术，或肖像总称；portrait 是一件作品。

entries.definition: To depict in a picture or words; portrait is the resulting noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在图画或文字中描绘；portrait 是结果名词。

entries.definition: A painter or photographer who specialises in portraits; the word names the person, not the work.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻肖像的画家或摄影师；这个名词指人，而非作品。

entries.definition: A portrait in which the artist depicts himself or herself; it is a compound of portrait with self.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术家描绘自己的肖像；是 portrait 与 self 的复合词。

entries.definition: The quality of looking like someone, or an image that resembles them; it need not be a formal portrait.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像某人的性质，或相似的形象；不一定是正式肖像。

entries.definition: A general visual representation; portrait specifies that the subject is a person.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指视觉再现；portrait 限定对象是人。

entries.definition: A sculpture of a person's head and shoulders; portrait includes painted, photographed and full-figure works.
entries.definitionCN: 人物头肩部的雕塑；portrait 还包括绘画、摄影与全身作品。

entries.definition: A side view of a face, or a short biographical sketch; a portrait may be frontal or in profile.
entries.definitionCN: 脸的侧面，或简短生平；肖像可以是正面或侧面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin protrahere 'draw forth' gives both portrait and portray.
normal.cn: 拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」同时给出 portrait 与 portray。

normal.en: The noun is a past participle turned into a thing: 'the drawn-out likeness'.
normal.cn: 这个名词是过去分词变成的物件：「被拉出的形象」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: portrait painter, family portrait, portrait mode.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：肖像画家、全家福、竖屏模式。

normal.en: The family runs portrait, portraiture, portraitist, portray and self-portrait.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 portrait、portraiture、portraitist、portray 与 self-portrait。

normal.en: A page taller than wide is in portrait format because portraits usually are.
normal.cn: 高大于宽的页面叫竖幅，因为肖像通常如此。

abstract.en: Picture a face held still while its look continues to move.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被固定住的脸，目光却仍在移动。

abstract.en: Picture a surface that can be paper, canvas, stone or a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一种可以是纸、画布、石头或屏幕的表面。

abstract.en: Picture a likeness that survives the person it shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个比被描绘者活得更久的形象。

examples.en: The portrait was cleaned and the varnish removed.
examples.cn: 这幅肖像经过清洗，清漆被去掉。

examples.en: He wrote a portrait of his father that avoided sentiment.
examples.cn: 他写下一篇避免感伤的父亲肖像。

examples.en: The stamp carries a portrait engraved from a photograph.
examples.cn: 这枚邮票上有一幅依据照片雕刻的肖像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「por（向前）+ trait（拉）」——把人的样子拉出来 → 肖像

root: 拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」（pro- 向前 + trahere 拉）经古法语 portraire、过去分词 portret，16 世纪 60 年代进入英语为 portrait；与 portray 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the drawn face to the photograph, the verbal description, the filmic place, the genre, any likeness, the vertical format and the sculpted bust.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从绘制的脸出发，转到照片、文字描写、影视地点、艺术门类、任何媒介的相似形象、竖幅版式与雕塑胸像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face is fixed in a pose while its gaze keeps looking outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张脸被固定在一个姿势里，目光却继续朝外看。

branches.en: THE LIKENESS IN MATTER: painted or sculpted, both aim at a recognisable person.
branches.cn: 材料中的形象：绘画或雕塑，目标都是可辨认的个人。

branches.en: THE CAMERA: the drawn likeness becomes a photographic one.
branches.cn: 相机：被绘制的形象变成照片。

branches.en: IN WORDS AND ON FILM: a person described, then a place given a face.
branches.cn: 文字与影片：先描写一个人，再给一个地方一张脸。

branches.en: CATEGORY AND MEDIUM: the genre, then any material that can carry it.
branches.cn: 类别与媒介：先是门类，再是任何能承载它的材料。

branches.en: FORMAT: the upright page inherits the shape of its usual subject.
branches.cn: 版式：竖幅页面继承了其常见题材的形状。

intro.en: Portrait is a Latin participle form borrowed through French; its family includes the verb of depicting and the name of the practice.
intro.cn: portrait 是经法语借入的拉丁分词形式；其词族包括描绘动词与指称这门实践的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin protrahere and trahere supply the root; the -trait ending is the French past-participle shape, not a living English suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 protrahere 与 trahere 提供词根；-trait 词尾是法语过去分词形态，不是能产的英语后缀。

items.example: The prefix contributes the sense of drawing out.
Trahere also gives tractor and trace.
items.exampleCN: trahere 还给出 tractor 与 trace。

items.example: The verb passed into English as portray.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词进入英语成为 portray。

items.structure: French portrait, past participle of portraire
items.example: The portrait was hung above the fireplace.
items.exampleCN: 这幅肖像挂在壁炉上方。

items.example: The novel portrays the city in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说描绘冬天的城市。

items.example: The portraitist worked only in pastel.
items.exampleCN: 这位肖像画家只用色粉。

items.example: The self-portrait shows the artist at work.
items.exampleCN: 这幅自画像表现正在作画的艺术家。

definition_zh: 造成（问题、威胁）；提出（问题）；摆姿势；冒充；放置；（名词）姿势；装出的样子
definition_en: to create a problem or threat; to ask a question; to hold a body position; to pretend to be something; (noun) a posture or a pretence
core_image: 把一件东西摆到台面上，让所有人都看见它在那儿
scene: 新规定给小农场主带来了严重的难题。The new regulations pose a serious problem for small farmers.
sceneCN: 这里 pose 是「造成、摆出（问题）」（第 1 个义项）；句意：新规定给小农户造成了严重问题。场景要点：问题被摆到台面上、无法回避；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 造成；提出；使摆好位置
摆姿势；装样子
姿势；装出的态度

derivatives.zh: 摆姿势的人；难题（英式口语 a poser）
摆姿势（的）；装样子的
装腔作势的人（经法语回流）
休息；安放（与 pose 同出 pausare 一线）

senses.title: To create a problem or difficulty
senses.titleCN: 造成：把问题摆到台面上
senses.definition: to create a problem, difficulty, or risk that others must deal with
senses.definitionCN: 造成别人必须应对的问题、困难或风险
senses.example: The new regulations pose a serious problem for small farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定给小农户造成了严重问题。
senses.why: The oldest concrete sense is to place something down. A problem that is posed is set in front of everyone, where it cannot be ignored.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的具体义是“放置”。被 pose 出来的问题，就是被摆到所有人面前、再也无法忽略的问题。

senses.title: To ask a question
senses.titleCN: 提出：把问题摆到对方面前
senses.definition: to put a question to someone, especially in a formal or public setting
senses.definitionCN: 向某人提出问题，尤指在正式或公开场合
senses.example: Reporters posed several questions about the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们就延期一事提出了几个问题。
senses.why: A question is placed before the person who must answer it. The same gesture of setting something down, now verbal.
senses.whyCN: 问题被放到必须作答的人面前。还是同一个“把东西放下”的动作，只是换成了言辞。

senses.title: To pretend to be something
senses.titleCN: 冒充：把自己摆成另一个身份
senses.definition: to claim or pretend to be a particular person or type of person
senses.definitionCN: 声称或假装自己是某个特定的人或某类人
senses.example: He posed as a security guard to get into the building.
senses.exampleCN: 他冒充保安进入了那栋楼。
senses.why: A pretender arranges his appearance in front of others, the way an object is placed for display. The identity is worn like a staged position.
senses.whyCN: 冒充者把自己的外观摆到别人眼前，就像把物件摆出来展示。身份被当成一个摆好的位置穿戴起来。

senses.title: To hold a body position
senses.titleCN: 摆姿势：把身体摆成一个造型
senses.definition: to hold one's body in a particular position, especially for a portrait or photograph
senses.definitionCN: 让身体保持某个特定姿势，尤指为了画像或拍照
senses.example: She posed for the portrait with one hand on the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 她一只手扶着椅子，为这幅肖像摆好姿势。
senses.why: Here the body itself is the object being placed. The painter arranges the sitter the way one arranges a still-life.
senses.whyCN: 这里被摆放的对象是身体本身。画家安排坐像的姿态，就像安排一组静物。

senses.title: To place something somewhere
senses.definition: to put or place something in a position, in formal or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到某个位置，用于正式或文学语体
senses.example: He posed the vase on the windowsill and stepped back.
senses.exampleCN: 他把花瓶放到窗台上，然后退后一步。
senses.why: This is the literal root meaning, the one from which every figurative sense borrows its picture.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的本义，所有引申义都是从这里借走那幅画面。

senses.title: Noun: a posture or attitude
senses.definition: a particular position of the body, or a way of behaving that is held for others to see
senses.definitionCN: 身体的某个特定姿势，或为了给别人看而保持的一种行为方式
senses.example: He struck a relaxed pose against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠在墙上，摆出一个放松的姿态。
senses.why: The verb's product becomes a noun: the position that has been placed and is now held.
senses.whyCN: 动词的产物变成名词：那个被摆好、并正在保持的位置。

senses.title: Noun: an affected manner
senses.definition: a way of behaving that is adopted to impress others and is not sincere
senses.definitionCN: 为了给别人留下印象而采用、并不真诚的行为方式
senses.example: His indifference was only a pose.
senses.exampleCN: 他的漠不关心只是装出来的。
senses.why: If a posture is deliberately arranged, it can also be a false one. The visible position no longer matches the inner state.
senses.whyCN: 既然姿态是被刻意安排出来的，它也就可以是假的。可见的位置不再与内在状态相符。

senses.title: To constitute a threat
senses.definition: to be a danger or menace to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物构成危险或威胁
senses.example: The invasive species poses a threat to native birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这种入侵物种对本地鸟类构成威胁。
senses.why: A threat is a problem aimed at someone. It is placed in their path, the same way an obstacle is placed on a road.
senses.whyCN: 威胁是冲着某人来的问题。它被摆到对方的路上，就像障碍被摆在道路中央。

intro.en: Pose came into English from French with the sense of placing. Its family history is tangled: a Latin verb meaning to pause lies behind it, while a different Latin verb meaning to place reshaped it.
intro.cn: pose 从法语进入英语，带着“放置”的意思。它的家族史相当缠绕：背后是一个意为“停顿”的拉丁动词，而另一个意为“放置”的拉丁动词又改造了它。

items.en: The French verb poser is generally traced to Vulgar Latin *pausare 'to halt, to rest', the same source as English pause and repose. The asterisk marks a reconstructed form, not a recorded one.
items.cn: 法语动词 poser 一般被追溯到通俗拉丁语 *pausare“停住、休息”，与英语 pause、repose 同源。星号表示这是重构形式，并非文献中实际记录的词。

items.en: Old French poser meant 'to put, place, set', and also 'to propose', especially in debating. Its placement sense is explained in the next item.
items.cn: 古法语 poser 意为“放、置、摆”，也指“提议”，尤用于辩论场合。其中“放置”义的来由见下一项。

items.en: Latin ponere, past participle positus, means 'to put, place', and its participle is the source of position, positive, deposit, and compose. Old French poser was not derived from it; rather, the similar stems were confused, and poser took over the 'place' sense. This is a documented case of confusion, not a shared root.
items.cn: 拉丁 ponere（过去分词 positus）意为“放置”，其分词是 position、positive、deposit、compose 的来源。古法语 poser 并非由它派生；真实情况是两个词干相似而被混同，poser 于是接管了“放置”义。这是有文献记载的混同，而非同源。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 14th century. Early senses include 'to suppose, to put forward', which survives in the phrase to pose a question.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入这个动词。早期义包括“设想、提出”，这层意思残存在 to pose a question 这一说法里。

items.en: The sense 'to hold a position for a portrait' develops later, and the noun pose, meaning a posture, is recorded in the early 19th century.
items.cn: “为画像保持某个姿势”的义项发展较晚；名词 pose（姿势）记录于 19 世纪初。

items.en: Modern English keeps both branches: placing (pose a question, pose a threat) and posturing (pose for a photo, a false pose). They meet in the same image of something set before the eyes.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了两支：放置（pose a question、pose a threat）与摆姿态（pose for a photo、a false pose）。两者汇合于同一个画面：某物被摆到眼前。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for placing, which is the hidden root behind much of this family. The second group collects verbs of putting forward and showing off.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“放置”的动词，它是这个词族背后隐藏的根。第二组收表示“提出”与“摆样子”的动词。

entries.definition: the place where something is, or a point of view. From Latin positio, from positus, the participle of ponere 'to place'.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所在的地点，或一种观点。来自拉丁 positio，再往上为 ponere“放置”的分词 positus。

entries.definition: the way the body is held. From Latin positura, also from ponere, and it overlaps with pose in the bodily sense.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的持姿方式。来自拉丁 positura，同样出自 ponere，在身体义上与 pose 重叠。

entries.definition: to put together, or to calm oneself. Com- 'together' plus ponere 'place': to place things together.
entries.definitionCN: 组合而成，或使镇定。com-“一起”加 ponere“放置”：把东西放在一起。

entries.definition: to put down, or money placed in a bank. De- 'down' plus positus: something placed down.
entries.definitionCN: 放下，或存入银行的钱。de-“向下”加 positus：被放下的东西。

entries.definition: to put something forward for consideration. Present is neutral and formal; pose often implies a difficulty or a challenge.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事提交考虑。present 中性而正式；pose 常含“造成困难或挑战”之意。

entries.definition: to bring up a question or issue. Raise is the common verb for questions; pose is slightly more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 提出一个问题或议题。raise 是提问题的常用动词；pose 稍正式。

entries.definition: to act as if something is true. Pretend is broader; pose as means adopt a false identity.
entries.definitionCN: 表现得好像某事为真。pretend 更宽；pose as 指冒充某个身份。

entries.definition: a deliberate bodily attitude, often used figuratively for political positioning. Posture is the more formal noun.
entries.definitionCN: 有意摆出的身体姿态，也常比喻政治上的站位。posture 是更正式的名词。

entries.definition: to put something in a position. Place is the plain everyday verb; pose in this sense is literary.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放在某个位置。place 是日常平实的动词；pose 的这个义项带文学色彩。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the object placed on the table, the question put to you, the fake uniform, the painter's sitter, and the borrowed pose.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：摆上桌的物件、推到你面前的问题、假制服、画家的模特、借来的姿态。

normal.en: Pose = place. Whatever is posed is put in front of you and stays there.
normal.cn: pose＝放置。凡被 pose 出来的，都摆在你面前，并且留在那儿。

normal.en: Pose a question: the question is physically set down between you and the person who must answer.
normal.cn: pose a question：问题被实打实地放在你和必须作答的人中间。

normal.en: Pose as a guard: you wear an identity the way you wear a uniform.
normal.cn: pose as a guard：你把身份穿在身上，就像穿上一套制服。

normal.en: Pose for a portrait: your body becomes the still-life the painter arranges.
normal.cn: pose for a portrait：你的身体成了画家摆布的那组静物。

normal.en: A pose can be sincere posture or a fake one; the noun covers both the stance and the act.
normal.cn: a pose 可以是真诚的姿态，也可以是假装的；这个名词同时覆盖“站姿”与“做戏”。

abstract.en: To pose a problem is to give it a location; what has no place can be ignored.
abstract.cn: 把问题 pose 出来，就是给它一个位置；没有位置的东西才能被忽略。

abstract.en: Every pose is a claim about where the body ends and the performance begins.
abstract.cn: 每一个姿态都在主张一件事：身体在哪里结束，表演从哪里开始。

abstract.en: The same gesture that sets a vase on a sill sets a question before a mind; placement is the common grammar of matter and speech.
abstract.cn: 把花瓶放上窗台与把问题放到心智面前，是同一个动作；放置是物质与言语共有的语法。

examples.en: The question posed by the audience was harder than any the professor had prepared for.
examples.cn: 听众提出的问题，比教授准备的任何一个都难。

examples.en: The model posed in silence while the students drew her.
examples.cn: 模特静静地摆着姿势，学生们画她。

examples.en: An empty warehouse poses no immediate danger, but it attracts trespassers.
examples.cn: 空仓库本身不构成直接危险，却会招来擅自进入的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: “剖姿”——把姿势剖开摆给众人看，就是 pose（摆姿势）；问题被摆出来，也叫 pose

root: 古法语 poser“放、置、提出”，一般追溯到通俗拉丁语 *pausare“停住、休息”（pause、repose 同源），其“放置”义很可能受拉丁 ponere／positum“放置”影响；英语 14 世纪借入。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense is a version of placing: a problem placed before people, a question placed before an answerer, a body placed for a painter, an identity placed over one's own. The noun is the position that results.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都是“放置”的一个版本：问题被放到众人面前，疑问被放到作答者面前，身体被摆给画家，身份被罩在自己身上。名词则是放置后形成的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands setting an object down where everyone can see it.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手把一件东西放下，放在所有人都看得见的地方。

chain: A PROBLEM OR QUESTION PUT FORTH

branches.en: BURDEN: a problem or threat placed in someone's path.
branches.cn: 负担：被摆到某人路上的问题或威胁。

branches.en: SPEECH: a question placed before the one who must answer.
branches.cn: 言语：被放到作答者面前的问题。

branches.en: FALSE FRONT: an identity or attitude arranged for others to see.
branches.cn: 假面：为给别人看而安排好的身份或态度。

branches.en: BODY: the sitter's position and the resulting posture.
branches.cn: 身体：模特的姿势与由此形成的体态。

branches.en: PLACEMENT: the literal act of putting an object somewhere.
branches.cn: 放置：把物件放到某处的字面动作。

intro.en: Pose sits at the meeting point of two Latin families: the pause family from *pausare, and the place family from ponere. English endings then built nouns and agents.
intro.cn: pose 处在两个拉丁词族的交汇处：来自 *pausare 的“停顿”族，以及来自 ponere 的“放置”族。英语词尾再构造出名词与施动者。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere and its participle positus supplied the place vocabulary; Vulgar Latin *pausare supplied the rest and resting vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere 及其分词 positus 提供了“放置”词汇；通俗拉丁 *pausare 提供了“休息、停驻”词汇。

definition_zh: 位置；方位；姿势；职位；立场；处境；安置；使处于
definition_en: the place where someone or something is, the way the body is arranged, a job, an opinion on an issue, a situation, or to put something in a particular place
core_image: 棋盘上一枚棋子被手指捏起，轻轻放进一个新的格子
scene: 比赛暂停时，教练把几枚棋子从棋盘边角挪到中央，又退后看了看。He moved the knight into a stronger position on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 position 是「位置」（第 1 个义项：某物所在的地方）；句意为他把马挪到棋盘上更有利的位置。图中可辨识物件：棋盘、棋子、教练。

pos.zh: 位置；方位；姿势；职位；立场；处境
安置；使处于（某位置）

derivatives.zh: 由 position 加 -al 构成，义为「位置的；与位置有关的」
由 position 加 -ing 构成，义为「定位；摆放」
由 position 加 -er 构成，义为「定位器；定位装置」

senses.title: The place where something is
senses.definition: the exact place where a person or thing is or should be
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物所在或应在的确切地点
senses.example: The map marks the position of every well in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 地图标出了山谷里每一口井的位置。
senses.why: Latin ponere means to place, and positio is a placing; the first sense is the result of that act, the spot where something has been put.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ponere 意为放置，positio 是「放置」这一动作；第一个义项就是动作的结果——某物被放定的那个点。

senses.title: The way the body is held
senses.definition: the way someone stands, sits or holds the body
senses.definitionCN: 人站立、坐着或摆放身体的方式
senses.example: Sit in a comfortable position with your back straight.
senses.exampleCN: 挺直背，以一种舒服的姿势坐好。
senses.why: A body placed this way or that forms a visible arrangement, so the placing word comes to name the shape the body makes.
senses.whyCN: 身体这样摆或那样摆，会形成看得见的安排；于是「放置」这个词开始指身体摆出的形状。

senses.title: A job or official role
senses.definition: a job in an organization, or the rank someone holds
senses.definitionCN: 在一个组织中的工作，或某人所居的级别
senses.example: She applied for a position in the research department.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了研究部的一个职位。
senses.why: A post is a place in an ordered structure: the person is placed in it, and the word for the placing becomes the word for the slot.
senses.whyCN: 职位是有序结构中的一个位置：人被放进这个位置，于是表示「放置」的词变成了表示「位置、空缺」的词。

senses.title: An opinion on an issue
senses.definition: the opinion someone takes on a question, especially one they are prepared to defend
senses.definitionCN: 某人对某个问题所持的看法，尤指愿意为之辩护的看法
senses.example: The committee took a firm position against the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会坚决反对修建这条新路。
senses.why: A standpoint is a place one stands; taking a position is choosing where to stand in an argument, so spatial placing turns into opinion.
senses.whyCN: 立场就是站的地方；表明立场就是在争论中选定站处，于是空间上的「放置」变成了看法。

senses.title: To put something in place
senses.definition: to put someone or something in a particular place or arrangement, often carefully
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物放到特定地点或安排中，往往带有仔细的意味
senses.example: He positioned the lamp so that the light fell on the page.
senses.exampleCN: 他把灯安置好，让光落在书页上。
senses.why: The noun names the resulting place; the verb is the act of producing it, and English formed the verb from the noun in modern times.
senses.whyCN: 名词指放置之后形成的位置；动词则是产生这个位置的动作，英语到近代才由名词造出这个动词。

intro.en: Position is the Latin verb ponere, to place, turned into a noun through its participle positus; English took it from French and later made a verb of it again.
intro.cn: position 是拉丁动词 ponere（放置）经其过去分词 positus 变成的名词；英语从法语借入，后来又把名词重新做成动词。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or place, and its past participle positus meant placed or set.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、安放，它的过去分词 positus 意为被放置的。

items.en: Positio was the abstract noun for a placing, and it could already mean the place a thing occupied.
items.cn: positio 是表示「放置」的抽象名词，当时已经可以指某物占据的位置。

items.en: Old French passed position to English in the fourteenth century as a word for a place or an arrangement.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把 position 传给英语，指位置或安排方式。

items.en: The word gained the senses of a military post, a job and a stated opinion, all built on the idea of a place one occupies.
items.cn: 这个词陆续获得军事据点、职位与明确看法等义项，全部建立在「所占之处」这一想法上。

items.en: Modern English formed the verb to position and added phrases such as market position, keeping the old placing core.
items.cn: 现代英语造出动词 to position，并添上 market position 一类说法，保留的仍是古老的「放置」核心。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb ponere; the near-meaning group gathers words for place, stance and job.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁动词 ponere 构成的词；近义组收表示地点、立场与职位的词。

entries.definition: Relating to position or place.
entries.definitionCN: 由 position 加 -al 构成，义为「位置的；与位置有关的」。

entries.definition: From Latin positivus and positus; it first meant placed or fixed, and now means affirmative.
entries.definitionCN: 与 positus 同根，原指被放置、被定下的，现代义为「肯定的」。

entries.definition: To put together, from com- plus ponere.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-（一起）与 ponere（放置）构成，义为「组成；创作」。

entries.definition: To put down, from de- plus ponere.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de-（向下）与 ponere（放置）构成，义为「存放；沉积」。

entries.definition: The place where something is.
entries.definitionCN: 位置；地点；强调地理上的所在，不指姿势或立场。

entries.definition: A public attitude towards an issue, or the way the body stands.
entries.definitionCN: 立场；站姿；同时覆盖态度与身体姿态。

entries.definition: A job or a place where someone is stationed.
entries.definitionCN: 职位；岗位；强调被派驻的工作地点。

entries.definition: The act of putting something in a place, or a job arranged for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 安置；安排；强调安排的动作或实习岗位。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on the Latin verb for placing, and its family keeps returning to spots, postures, posts and stands.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词立足于拉丁语表示「放置」的动词，同族词反复回到地点、姿势、职位与立场。

normal.en: Ponere means to place, and its participle positus is the stem behind position, positive and posit.
normal.cn: ponere 意为放置，它的过去分词 positus 正是 position、positive 与 posit 共同的词干。

normal.en: Compose is com- plus ponere, to put together; deposit is de- plus ponere, to put down.
normal.cn: compose 是 com- 加 ponere，意为放在一起；deposit 是 de- 加 ponere，意为放下。

normal.en: Positional adds -al and simply describes anything about place or arrangement.
normal.cn: positional 加 -al，只用来描述与位置或安排有关的事物。

normal.en: A job is a position because a person is placed into a slot in an organization.
normal.cn: 职位之所以叫 position，是因为人被放进组织中的一个格子里。

normal.en: A position in an argument is a place to stand, which is why one word covers location and opinion.
normal.cn: 争论中的立场就是站的地方，所以一个词同时覆盖位置与看法。

abstract.en: A position is where you are, but also where you choose to stand, and English lets one word hold both.
abstract.cn: 位置既是你所在之处，也是你选择站立之处，英语让一个词同时装下两者。

abstract.en: On a board every piece has a position, and changing it changes what the piece can do.
abstract.cn: 棋盘上每枚棋子都有位置，改变位置就改变了它所能做的事。

abstract.en: To be in position is to be ready, which is why the word appears in sports, jobs and arguments alike.
abstract.cn: 就位就是准备好了，所以这个词在体育、职场与争论里都会出现。

examples.en: He moved the knight into a stronger position on the board.
examples.cn: 他把马挪到棋盘上更有利的位置。

examples.en: She applied for a position in the research department.
examples.cn: 她申请了研究部的一个职位。

examples.en: The committee took a firm position against the new road.
examples.cn: 委员会坚决反对修建这条新路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡贼神」——把棋子摆到棋盘上的某一点，那个点就定了；position 就是位置，也是职位与立场。

root: 源自拉丁 ponere（放置）的过去分词 positus，再由抽象名词 positio 经古法语进入英语；同族词有 compose、deposit、positive。注意与来自 portare（搬运）的 port、portable 区分：position 的核心是「放」，不是「搬」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place something occupies; the senses branch into physical location, body posture, a job slot, a standpoint, and the act of placing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是某物所占据的地方；义项由此分出物理位置、身体姿势、职位空缺、立场，以及放置的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chess piece lifted between two fingers and set down in a new square.
core.cn: 核心意象：棋盘上一枚棋子被手指捏起，轻轻放进一个新的格子。

branches.en: a marker pinned to a spot on a map
branches.cn: 钉在地图某点上的标记

branches.en: a back held straight in a chair
branches.cn: 椅子上挺直的背

branches.en: a name written into an empty slot on an org chart
branches.cn: 组织架构图空格里写下的名字

branches.en: a delegate standing to state a view
branches.cn: 代表站起来陈述看法

branches.en: a camera positioned to catch the whole stage
branches.cn: 被安放好以拍到整个舞台的相机

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin verb for placing, its participle and an action suffix, and the same pieces also build compose and deposit.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「放置」动词、它的过去分词与一个动作名词后缀构成，同样的部件还造出了 compose 与 deposit。

latinIntro.en: Position comes from Latin ponere, to place, through its participle positus and the noun positio; the same verb also gives compose and deposit.
latinIntro.cn: position 来自拉丁 ponere（放置），经由过去分词 positus 与名词 positio；同一个动词还给出 compose 与 deposit。

definition_zh: 积极的；肯定的；正面的；确凿的；阳性的；正的；正电的；原级
definition_en: optimistic or hopeful; expressing agreement or certainty; showing that something is present; (of a number or charge) above zero
core_image: 在一张横轴上，站在零点右边，并明确说「是」
scene: 即使被第三次拒绝，她依然保持积极。She stayed positive even after the third rejection.
sceneCN: 这里 positive 是「心态积极的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：即使被拒三次，她仍然保持积极。场景要点：方向朝上、向前看、不垮；对应第 1 个义项。

正面之处；正数；（摄影）正片

积极性；乐观；阳性
